Then there was another beast, a second one, like a bear. It was raised up on one side, and it had three ribs in its mouth between its teeth. It was told, 'Get up, devour much flesh!'
וַאֲר֣וּ חֵיוָה֩ אָחֳרִ֨י תִנְיָנָ֜ה דָּמְיָ֣ה לְדֹ֗ב וְלִשְׂטַר־חַד֙ הֳקִמַ֔ת וּתְלָ֥ת עִלְעִ֛ין בְּפֻמַּ֖הּ בֵּ֣ין *שניה **שִׁנַּ֑הּ וְכֵן֙ אָמְרִ֣ין לַ֔הּ ק֥וּמִֽי אֲכֻ֖לִי בְּשַׂ֥ר שַׂגִּֽיא׃
After this I looked, and there was another, like a leopard. It had four wings of a bird on its back, and the beast had four heads, and it was given authority to rule.
בָּאתַ֨ר דְּנָ֜ה חָזֵ֣ה הֲוֵ֗ית וַאֲר֤וּ אָֽחֳרִי֙ כִּנְמַ֔ר וְלַ֨הּ גַּפִּ֥ין אַרְבַּ֛ע דִּי־ע֖וֹף עַל־*גביה **גַּבַּ֑הּ וְאַרְבְּעָ֤ה רֵאשִׁין֙ לְחֵ֣יוְתָ֔א וְשָׁלְטָ֖ן יְהִ֥יב לַֽהּ׃

After this I was looking in the visions of the night, and there was a fourth beast, terrifying and dreadful and extremely strong. It had great iron teeth. It devoured and crushed, and it trampled what was left with its feet. It was different from all the beasts before it, and it had ten horns.

בָּאתַ֣ר דְּנָה֩ חָזֵ֨ה הֲוֵ֜ית בְּחֶזְוֵ֣י לֵֽילְיָ֗א וַאֲר֣וּ חֵיוָ֣ה *רביעיה **רְֽבִיעָאָ֡ה דְּחִילָה֩ וְאֵֽימְתָנִ֨י וְתַקִּיפָ֜א יַתִּ֗ירָא וְשִׁנַּ֨יִן דִּֽי־פַרְזֶ֥ל לַהּ֙ רַבְרְבָ֔ן אָֽכְלָ֣ה וּמַדֱּקָ֔ה וּשְׁאָרָ֖א *ברגליה **בְּרַגְלַ֣הּ רָפְסָ֑ה וְהִ֣יא מְשַׁנְּיָ֗ה מִן־כָּל־חֵֽיוָתָא֙ דִּ֣י קֽ͏ָדָמַ֔יהּ וְקַרְנַ֥יִן עֲשַׂ֖ר לַֽהּ׃

While I was considering the horns, there was another horn, a small one, coming up among them, and three of the first horns were uprooted before it. This horn had eyes like human eyes and a mouth speaking arrogant words.[^4]

מִשְׂתַּכַּ֨ל הֲוֵ֜ית בְּקַרְנַיָּ֗א וַ֠אֲלוּ קֶ֣רֶן אָחֳרִ֤י זְעֵירָה֙ סִלְקָ֣ת *ביניהון **בֵּֽינֵיהֵ֔ן וּתְלָ֗ת מִן־קַרְנַיָּא֙ קַדְמָ֣יָתָ֔א *אתעקרו **אֶתְעֲקַ֖רָה מִן־*קדמיה **קֳדָמַ֑הּ וַאֲל֨וּ עַיְנִ֜ין כְּעַיְנֵ֤י אֲנָשָׁא֙ בְּקַרְנָא־דָ֔א וּפֻ֖ם מְמַלִּ֥ל רַבְרְבָֽן׃

As I looked, thrones were set in place, and the Ancient of Days[^5] took his seat. His clothing was white as snow, and the hair of his head like pure wool. His throne was flames of fire, and its wheels were burning fire.

חָזֵ֣ה הֲוֵ֗ית עַ֣ד דִּ֤י כָרְסָוָן֙ רְמִ֔יו וְעַתִּ֥יק יוֹמִ֖ין יְתִ֑ב לְבוּשֵׁ֣הּ ׀ כִּתְלַ֣ג חִוָּ֗ר וּשְׂעַ֤ר רֵאשֵׁהּ֙ כַּעֲמַ֣ר נְקֵ֔א כָּרְסְיֵהּ֙ שְׁבִיבִ֣ין דִּי־נ֔וּר גַּלְגִּלּ֖וֹהִי נ֥וּר דָּלִֽק׃

A river of fire was flowing, coming out from before him. Thousands upon thousands served him, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before him.[^6] The court sat in judgment, and the books were opened.
נְהַ֣ר דִּי־נ֗וּר נָגֵ֤ד וְנָפֵק֙ מִן־קֳדָמ֔וֹהִי אֶ֤לֶף *אלפים **אַלְפִין֙ יְשַׁמְּשׁוּנֵּ֔הּ וְרִבּ֥וֹ *רבון **רִבְבָ֖ן קֽ͏ָדָמ֣וֹהִי יְקוּמ֑וּן דִּינָ֥א יְתִ֖ב וְסִפְרִ֥ין פְּתִֽיחוּ׃
Then I kept looking because of the sound of the arrogant words that the horn was speaking. As I watched, the beast was killed, and its body destroyed and given over to the burning fire.
חָזֵ֣ה הֲוֵ֔ית בֵּאדַ֗יִן מִן־קָל֙ מִלַּיָּ֣א רַבְרְבָתָ֔א דִּ֥י קַרְנָ֖א מְמַלֱּלָ֑ה חָזֵ֣ה הֲוֵ֡ית עַד֩ דִּ֨י קְטִילַ֤ת חֵֽיוְתָא֙ וְהוּבַ֣ד גִּשְׁמַ֔הּ וִיהִיבַ֖ת לִיקֵדַ֥ת אֶשָּֽׁא׃
As for the rest of the beasts, their authority was taken away, but their lives were prolonged for a season and a time.
וּשְׁאָר֙ חֵֽיוָתָ֔א הֶעְדִּ֖יו שָׁלְטָנְה֑וֹן וְאַרְכָ֧ה בְחַיִּ֛ין יְהִ֥יבַת לְה֖וֹן עַד־זְמַ֥ן וְעִדָּֽן׃
I was looking in the visions of the night, and there, with the clouds of heaven, one like a son of man[^7] was coming. He came to the Ancient of Days and was presented before him.
חָזֵ֤ה הֲוֵית֙ בְּחֶזְוֵ֣י לֵֽילְיָ֔א וַאֲרוּ֙ עִם־עֲנָנֵ֣י שְׁמַיָּ֔א כְּבַ֥ר אֱנָ֖שׁ אָתֵ֣ה הֲוָ֑ה וְעַד־עַתִּ֤יק יֽוֹמַיָּא֙ מְטָ֔ה וּקְדָמ֖וֹהִי הַקְרְבֽוּהִי׃

He was given authority, glory and kingship, so that all peoples, nations and languages would serve him.[^8] His authority is an everlasting authority that will not pass away, and his kingdom is one that will not be destroyed.
וְלֵ֨ה יְהִ֤יב שָׁלְטָן֙ וִיקָ֣ר וּמַלְכ֔וּ וְכֹ֣ל עַֽמְמַיָּ֗א אֻמַיָּ֛א וְלִשָּׁנַיָּ֖א לֵ֣הּ יִפְלְח֑וּן שָׁלְטָנֵ֞הּ שָׁלְטָ֤ן עָלַם֙ דִּֽי־לָ֣א יֶעְדֵּ֔ה וּמַלְכוּתֵ֖הּ דִּי־לָ֥א תִתְחַבַּֽל׃ פ
As for me, Daniel, my spirit was distressed within me,[^9] and the visions that passed through my head terrified me.
אֶתְכְּרִיַּ֥ת רוּחִ֛י אֲנָ֥ה דָנִיֵּ֖אל בְּג֣וֹא נִדְנֶ֑ה וְחֶזְוֵ֥י רֵאשִׁ֖י יְבַהֲלֻנַּֽנִי׃
I approached one of those standing there and asked him the truth about all this. So he told me and made known to me the interpretation of these things:
קִרְבֵ֗ת עַל־חַד֙ מִן־קָ֣אֲמַיָּ֔א וְיַצִּיבָ֥א אֶבְעֵֽא־מִנֵּ֖הּ עַֽל־כָּל־דְּנָ֑ה וַאֲמַר־לִ֕י וּפְשַׁ֥ר מִלַּיָּ֖א יְהוֹדְעִנַּֽנִי׃
'These great beasts, which are four, are four kings who will arise from the earth.
אִלֵּין֙ חֵיוָתָ֣א רַבְרְבָתָ֔א דִּ֥י אִנִּ֖ין אַרְבַּ֑ע אַרְבְּעָ֥ה מַלְכִ֖ין יְקוּמ֥וּן מִן־אַרְעָֽא׃
But the holy ones of the Most High[^10] will receive the kingdom, and they will possess the kingdom forever, forever and ever.'
וִֽיקַבְּלוּן֙ מַלְכוּתָ֔א קַדִּישֵׁ֖י עֶלְיוֹנִ֑ין וְיַחְסְנ֤וּן מַלְכוּתָא֙ עֽ͏ַד־עָ֣לְמָ֔א וְעַ֖ד עָלַ֥ם עָלְמַיָּֽא׃

Then I wanted to know the truth about the fourth beast, which was different from all the others, extremely terrifying, with teeth of iron and claws of bronze, which devoured and crushed and trampled what was left with its feet,

אֱדַ֗יִן צְבִית֙ לְיַצָּבָ֔[t]א עַל־חֵֽיוְתָא֙ רְבִיעָ֣יְתָ֔א דִּֽי־הֲוָ֥ת שָֽׁנְיָ֖ה מִן־*כלהון **כָּלְּהֵ֑ין דְּחִילָ֣ה יַתִּ֗ירָה *שניה **שִׁנַּ֤הּ דִּֽי פַרְזֶל֙ וְטִפְרַ֣יהּ דִּֽי־נְחָ֔שׁ אָֽכְלָ֣ה מַדֲּקָ֔ה וּשְׁאָרָ֖א בְּרַגְלַ֥יהּ רָֽפְסָֽה׃
and about the ten horns on its head, and the other horn that came up, before which three fell: the horn that had eyes and a mouth speaking arrogant words, and that looked greater than the others.

וְעַל־קַרְנַיָּ֤א עֲשַׂר֙ דִּ֣י בְרֵאשַׁ֔הּ וְאָחֳרִי֙ דִּ֣י סִלְקַ֔ת *ונפלו **וּנְפַ֥לָה מִן־*קדמיה **קֳדָמַ֖הּ תְּלָ֑ת וְקַרְנָ֨א דִכֵּ֜ן וְעַיְנִ֣ין לַ֗הּ וְפֻם֙ מְמַלִּ֣ל רַבְרְבָ֔ן וְחֶזְוַ֖הּ רַ֥ב מִן־חַבְרָתַֽהּ׃
As I watched, this horn was making war against the holy ones and was prevailing over them,
חָזֵ֣ה הֲוֵ֔ית וְקַרְנָ֣א דִכֵּ֔ן עָבְדָ֥ה קְרָ֖ב עִם־קַדִּישִׁ֑ין וְיָכְלָ֖ה לְהֽוֹן׃
until the Ancient of Days came and judgment was given in favor of the holy ones of the Most High,[^11] and the time came when the holy ones took possession of the kingdom.
עַ֣ד דִּֽי־אֲתָ֗ה עַתִּיק֙ יֽוֹמַיָּ֔א וְדִינָ֣א יְהִ֔ב לְקַדִּישֵׁ֖י עֶלְיוֹנִ֑ין וְזִמְנָ֣א מְטָ֔ה וּמַלְכוּתָ֖א הֶחֱסִ֥נוּ קַדִּישִֽׁין׃
This is what he said: 'The fourth beast will be a fourth kingdom on earth, which will be different from all the kingdoms. It will devour the whole earth, trample it down and crush it.
כֵּן֮ אֲמַר֒ חֵֽיוְתָא֙ רְבִיעָ֣יְתָ֔א מַלְכ֤וּ *רביעיא **רְבִיעָאָה֙ תֶּהֱוֵ֣א בְאַרְעָ֔א דִּ֥י תִשְׁנֵ֖א מִן־כָּל־מַלְכְוָתָ֑א וְתֵאכֻל֙ כָּל־אַרְעָ֔א וּתְדוּשִׁנַּ֖הּ וְתַדְּקִנַּֽהּ׃
As for the ten horns, out of this kingdom ten kings will arise, and another will arise after them. He will be different from the earlier ones, and he will bring down three kings.
וְקַרְנַיָּ֣א עֲשַׂ֔ר מִנַּהּ֙ מַלְכוּתָ֔ה עַשְׂרָ֥ה מַלְכִ֖ין יְקֻמ֑וּן וְאָחֳרָ֞ן יְק֣וּם אַחֲרֵיה֗וֹן וְה֤וּא יִשְׁנֵא֙ מִן־קַדְמָיֵ֔א וּתְלָתָ֥ה מַלְכִ֖ין יְהַשְׁפִּֽל׃

He will speak words against the Most High and wear down the holy ones of the Most High. He will try to change the sacred seasons and the law,[^12] and they will be given into his hand for a time, times and half a time.[^13]
וּמִלִּ֗ין לְצַ֤ד *עליא **עִלָּאָה֙ יְמַלִּ֔ל וּלְקַדִּישֵׁ֥י עֶלְיוֹנִּ֖ין יְבַלֵּ֑א וְיִסְבַּ֗ר לְהַשְׁנָיָה֙ זִמְנִ֣ין וְדָ֔ת וְיִתְיַהֲב֣וּן בִּידֵ֔הּ עַד־עִדָּ֥ן וְעִדָּנִ֖ין וּפְלַ֥ג עִדָּֽן׃
But the court will sit in judgment, and his authority will be taken away, to be destroyed and abolished forever.
וְדִינָ֖א יִתִּ֑ב וְשָׁלְטָנֵ֣הּ יְהַעְדּ֔וֹן לְהַשְׁמָדָ֥ה וּלְהוֹבָדָ֖ה עַד־סוֹפָֽא׃

Then the kingship and the authority and the greatness of the kingdoms under the whole heaven will be given to the people of the holy ones of the Most High. Their kingdom will be an everlasting kingdom, and all rulers will serve and obey them.'[^14]

וּמַלְכוּתָ֨ה וְשָׁלְטָנָ֜א וּרְבוּתָ֗א דִּ֚י מַלְכְוָת֙ תְּח֣וֹת כָּל־שְׁמַיָּ֔א יְהִיבַ֕ת לְעַ֖ם קַדִּישֵׁ֣י עֶלְיוֹנִ֑ין מַלְכוּתֵהּ֙ מַלְכ֣וּת עָלַ֔ם וְכֹל֙ שָׁלְטָ֣נַיָּ֔א לֵ֥הּ יִפְלְח֖וּן וְיִֽשְׁתַּמְּעֽוּן׃
Here is the end of the account. As for me, Daniel, my thoughts greatly terrified me, and my face turned pale, but I kept the matter in my heart."
עַד־כָּ֖ה סוֹפָ֣א דִֽי־מִלְּתָ֑א אֲנָ֨ה דָֽנִיֵּ֜אל שַׂגִּ֣יא ׀ רַעְיוֹנַ֣י יְבַהֲלֻנַּ֗נִי וְזִיוַי֙ יִשְׁתַּנּ֣וֹן עֲלַ֔י וּמִלְּתָ֖א בְּלִבִּ֥י נִטְרֵֽת׃ פ

n.1: Perhaps about 550 BC, when Nabonidus left Belshazzar in charge of Babylon (see 5:1).
n.2: Literally "he said the head of the words". The meaning of the Aramaic is uncertain.
n.4: Literally "great things". Also in verses 11 and 20.
n.5: Aramaic *attiq yomin*, "one advanced in days", an aged figure: God seated as judge. Here the phrase has no article ("one ancient of days"); in verses 13 and 22 it is "the Ancient of Days".
n.6: Literally "A thousand thousands served him, and a myriad of myriads stood before him".
n.7: Aramaic *kevar enash*, "like a son of man", that is, one in human form, in contrast to the beasts. *Bar enash*, like Hebrew *ben adam*, means "a human being" (compare 8:17). In the interpretation (verses 18, 22 and 27) the kingdom is given to "the holy ones of the Most High". Interpreters have understood the figure as a symbol of God's faithful people, as an angel such as Michael (10:21; 12:1), or as a heavenly ruler. Later Jewish writings (1 Enoch 37–71; 4 Ezra 13) and some rabbinic teachers took him to be the Messiah. In the Gospels, Jesus' title "the Son of Man" draws on this verse (Mark 13:26; 14:62), and Revelation 1:7, 13 alludes to it.
n.8: Aramaic *pelach*, "serve", the verb used for serving God or the gods (3:12, 14, 17–18, 28; 6:17, 21). Also in verse 27.
n.9: Literally "within its sheath", the body as the sheath of the spirit.
n.10: Aramaic *qaddishe elyonin*. In the Old Testament "holy ones" usually means angels (4:10, 14; 8:13; Psalm 89:6, 8), but here it may mean God's faithful people (compare verse 27, "the people of the holy ones of the Most High"). *Elyonin*, "Most High", is plural in form, probably as a mark of majesty. Also in verses 22, 25 and 27.
n.11: Or "the right to judge was given to the holy ones of the Most High".
n.12: Literally "the times and the law", probably the sacred calendar and festivals and the law of God. Many interpreters identify the small horn with Antiochus IV Epiphanes, king of the Seleucid empire from 175 to 164 BC, who banned the Jewish festivals and the observance of the Law (1 Maccabees 1:41–64; compare Daniel 8:9–12; 11:21–45). Others see a later ruler.
n.13: That is, probably three and a half years. Compare 12:7 and Revelation 12:14.
n.14: Literally "His kingdom … serve and obey him". The singular pronoun may refer to the people or to the Most High.

v: In the third year of the reign of King Belshazzar, a vision appeared to me, Daniel, after the one that had appeared to me before.[^1]
בִּשְׁנַ֣ת שָׁל֔וֹשׁ לְמַלְכ֖וּת בֵּלְאשַׁצַּ֣ר הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ חָז֞וֹן נִרְאָ֤ה אֵלַי֙ אֲנִ֣י דָנִיֵּ֔אל אַחֲרֵ֛י הַנִּרְאָ֥ה אֵלַ֖י בַּתְּחִלָּֽה׃
I looked in the vision, and as I looked, I was in the fortress of Susa,[^2] in the province of Elam. I looked in the vision, and I was beside the Ulai Canal.[^3]
וָֽאֶרְאֶה֮ בֶּחָזוֹן֒ וַיְהִי֙ בִּרְאֹתִ֔י וַאֲנִי֙ בְּשׁוּשַׁ֣ן הַבִּירָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּעֵילָ֣ם הַמְּדִינָ֑ה וָאֶרְאֶה֙ בֶּֽחָז֔וֹן וַאֲנִ֥י הָיִ֖יתִי עַל־אוּבַ֥ל אוּלָֽי׃
I lifted my eyes and looked, and there was a ram standing beside the canal. It had two horns. Both horns were long, but one was longer than the other, and the longer one came up last.
וָאֶשָּׂ֤א עֵינַי֙ וָאֶרְאֶ֔ה וְהִנֵּ֣ה ׀ אַ֣יִל אֶחָ֗ד עֹמֵ֛ד לִפְנֵ֥י הָאֻבָ֖ל וְל֣וֹ קְרָנָ֑יִם וְהַקְּרָנַ֣יִם גְּבֹה֗וֹת וְהָאַחַת֙ גְּבֹהָ֣ה מִן־הַשֵּׁנִ֔ית וְהַ֨גְּבֹהָ֔ה עֹלָ֖ה בָּאַחֲרֹנָֽה׃
I saw the ram charging westward, northward and southward. No beast could stand before it, and there was no one who could rescue from its power. It did as it pleased and made itself great.
רָאִ֣יתִי אֶת־הָאַ֡יִל מְנַגֵּחַ֩ יָ֨מָּה וְצָפ֜וֹנָה וָנֶ֗גְבָּה וְכָל־חַיּוֹת֙ לֹֽא־יַֽעַמְד֣וּ לְפָנָ֔יו וְאֵ֥ין מַצִּ֖יל מִיָּד֑וֹ וְעָשָׂ֥ה כִרְצֹנ֖וֹ וְהִגְדִּֽיל׃
As I was considering this, a male goat came from the west across the face of the whole earth, without touching the ground. The goat had a conspicuous horn between its eyes.
וַאֲנִ֣י ׀ הָיִ֣יתִי מֵבִ֗ין וְהִנֵּ֤ה צְפִיר־הָֽעִזִּים֙ בָּ֤א מִן־הַֽמַּעֲרָב֙ עַל־פְּנֵ֣י כָל־הָאָ֔רֶץ וְאֵ֥ין נוֹגֵ֖עַ בָּאָ֑רֶץ וְהַ֨צָּפִ֔יר קֶ֥רֶן חָז֖וּת בֵּ֥ין עֵינָֽיו׃
It came to the ram with the two horns, which I had seen standing beside the canal, and it charged at it in furious strength.
וַיָּבֹ֗א עַד־הָאַ֙יִל֙ בַּ֣עַל הַקְּרָנַ֔יִם אֲשֶׁ֣ר רָאִ֔יתִי עֹמֵ֖ד לִפְנֵ֣י הָאֻבָ֑ל וַיָּ֥רָץ אֵלָ֖יו בַּחֲמַ֥ת כֹּחֽוֹ׃

I saw it reach the ram. It was enraged against it, and it struck the ram and broke its two horns. The ram had no strength to stand before it. It threw the ram to the ground and trampled on it, and there was no one who could rescue the ram from its power.

וּרְאִיתִ֞יו מַגִּ֣יעַ ׀ אֵ֣צֶל הָאַ֗יְל וַיִּתְמַרְמַ֤ר אֵלָיו֙ וַיַּ֣ךְ אֶת־הָאַ֗יִל וַיְשַׁבֵּר֙ אֶת־שְׁתֵּ֣י קְרָנָ֔יו וְלֹא־הָ֥יָה כֹ֛חַ בָּאַ֖יִל לַעֲמֹ֣ד לְפָנָ֑יו וַיַּשְׁלִיכֵ֤הוּ אַ֙רְצָה֙ וַֽיִּרְמְסֵ֔הוּ וְלֹא־הָיָ֥ה מַצִּ֛יל לָאַ֖יִל מִיָּדֽוֹ׃
The male goat made itself very great. But at the height of its power the great horn was broken, and in its place four conspicuous horns came up toward the four winds of heaven.
וּצְפִ֥יר הָעִזִּ֖ים הִגְדִּ֣יל עַד־מְאֹ֑ד וּכְעָצְמ֗וֹ נִשְׁבְּרָה֙ הַקֶּ֣רֶן הַגְּדוֹלָ֔ה וַֽתַּעֲלֶ֜נָה חָז֤וּת אַרְבַּע֙ תַּחְתֶּ֔יהָ לְאַרְבַּ֖ע רוּח֥וֹת הַשָּׁמָֽיִם׃
Out of one of them came another horn, a small one,[^4] which grew exceedingly great toward the south, toward the east and toward the beautiful land.[^5]
וּמִן־הָאַחַ֣ת מֵהֶ֔ם יָצָ֥א קֶֽרֶן־אַחַ֖ת מִצְּעִירָ֑ה וַתִּגְדַּל־יֶ֛תֶר אֶל־הַנֶּ֥גֶב וְאֶל־הַמִּזְרָ֖ח וְאֶל־הַצֶּֽבִי׃
It grew as high as the host of heaven, and it threw down to the earth some of the host and some of the stars, and trampled on them.
וַתִּגְדַּ֖ל עַד־צְבָ֣א הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם וַתַּפֵּ֥ל אַ֛רְצָה מִן־הַצָּבָ֥א וּמִן־הַכּוֹכָבִ֖ים וַֽתִּרְמְסֵֽם׃
It made itself great, even up to the commander of the host.[^6] The regular offering was taken away from him,[^7] and the place of his sanctuary was thrown down.
וְעַ֥ד שַֽׂר־הַצָּבָ֖א הִגְדִּ֑יל וּמִמֶּ֙נּוּ֙ *הרים **הוּרַ֣ם הַתָּמִ֔יד וְהֻשְׁלַ֖ךְ מְכ֥וֹן מִקְדָּשֽׁוֹ׃
Because of transgression, the host was given over, together with the regular offering.[^8] It threw truth to the ground, and it acted and succeeded.
וְצָבָ֛א תִּנָּתֵ֥ן עַל־הַתָּמִ֖יד בְּפָ֑שַׁע וְתַשְׁלֵ֤ךְ אֱמֶת֙ אַ֔רְצָה וְעָשְׂתָ֖ה וְהִצְלִֽיחָה׃

Then I heard a holy one speaking, and another holy one said to the one who was speaking,[^9] "How long will the vision last, concerning the regular offering, the transgression that makes desolate,[^10] and the giving over of both the sanctuary and the host to be trampled?"
וָאֶשְׁמְעָ֥ה אֶֽחָד־קָד֖וֹשׁ מְדַבֵּ֑ר וַיֹּאמֶר֩ אֶחָ֨ד קָד֜וֹשׁ לַפַּֽלְמוֹנִ֣י הַֽמְדַבֵּ֗ר עַד־מָתַ֞י הֶחָז֤וֹן הַתָּמִיד֙ וְהַפֶּ֣שַׁע שֹׁמֵ֔ם תֵּ֛ת וְקֹ֥דֶשׁ וְצָבָ֖א מִרְמָֽס׃
He said to me,[^11] "For 2,300 evenings and mornings.[^12] Then the sanctuary will be restored to its rightful state."[^13]
וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֔י עַ֚ד עֶ֣רֶב בֹּ֔קֶר אַלְפַּ֖יִם וּשְׁלֹ֣שׁ מֵא֑וֹת וְנִצְדַּ֖ק קֹֽדֶשׁ׃
While I, Daniel, was seeing the vision and trying to understand it, there stood before me one who looked like a man.[^14]
וַיְהִ֗י בִּרְאֹתִ֛י אֲנִ֥י דָנִיֵּ֖אל אֶת־הֶחָז֑וֹן וָאֲבַקְשָׁ֣ה בִינָ֔ה וְהִנֵּ֛ה עֹמֵ֥ד לְנֶגְדִּ֖י כְּמַרְאֵה־גָֽבֶר׃
And I heard a human voice from between the banks of the Ulai, and it called out, "Gabriel,[^15] make this man understand the vision."
וָאֶשְׁמַ֥ע קוֹל־אָדָ֖ם בֵּ֣ין אוּלָ֑י וַיִּקְרָא֙ וַיֹּאמַ֔ר גַּבְרִיאֵ֕ל הָבֵ֥ן לְהַלָּ֖ז אֶת־הַמַּרְאֶֽה׃
He came near where I stood, and when he came I was terrified and fell on my face. He said to me, "Understand, son of man,[^16] that the vision is for the time of the end."
וַיָּבֹא֙ אֵ֣צֶל עָמְדִ֔י וּבְבֹא֣וֹ נִבְעַ֔תִּי וָאֶפְּלָ֖ה עַל־פָּנָ֑י וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלַי֙ הָבֵ֣ן בֶּן־אָדָ֔ם כִּ֖י לְעֶת־קֵ֥ץ הֶחָזֽוֹן׃
While he was speaking with me, I fell into a deep sleep with my face to the ground. Then he touched me and set me on my feet.[^17]
וּבְדַבְּר֣וֹ עִמִּ֔י נִרְדַּ֥מְתִּי עַל־פָּנַ֖י אָ֑רְצָה וַיִּ֨גַּע־בִּ֔י וַיַּֽעֲמִידֵ֖נִי עַל־עָמְדִֽי׃
He said, "I am going to make known to you what will happen at the end of the time of wrath,[^18] for it concerns the appointed time of the end.[^19]
וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ הִנְנִ֣י מוֹדִֽיעֲךָ֔ אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־יִהְיֶ֖ה בְּאַחֲרִ֣ית הַזָּ֑עַם כִּ֖י לְמוֹעֵ֥ד קֵֽץ׃
The ram that you saw with the two horns: these are the kings of Media and Persia.
הָאַ֥יִל אֲשֶׁר־רָאִ֖יתָ בַּ֣עַל הַקְּרָנָ֑יִם מַלְכֵ֖י מָדַ֥י וּפָרָֽס׃
The shaggy male goat is the king of Greece,[^20] and the great horn between its eyes is the first king.[^21]
וְהַצָּפִ֥יר הַשָּׂעִ֖יר מֶ֣לֶךְ יָוָ֑ן וְהַקֶּ֤רֶן הַגְּדוֹלָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בֵּין־עֵינָ֔יו ה֖וּא הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ הָרִאשֽׁוֹן׃
As for the horn that was broken and the four that arose in its place: four kingdoms will arise from his nation, but not with his power.[^22]
וְהַ֨נִּשְׁבֶּ֔רֶת וַתַּֽעֲמֹ֥דְנָה אַרְבַּ֖ע תַּחְתֶּ֑יהָ אַרְבַּ֧ע מַלְכֻי֛וֹת מִגּ֥וֹי יַעֲמֹ֖דְנָה וְלֹ֥א בְכֹחֽוֹ׃
At the end of their rule, when the transgressors have reached their full measure, a king will arise, fierce-looking and skilled in intrigue.[^23]
וּֽבְאַחֲרִית֙ מַלְכוּתָ֔ם כְּהָתֵ֖ם הַפֹּשְׁעִ֑ים יַעֲמֹ֛ד מֶ֥לֶךְ עַז־פָּנִ֖ים וּמֵבִ֥ין חִידֽוֹת׃
His power will be mighty, but not by his own power. He will cause astonishing destruction,[^24] and he will succeed in what he does. He will destroy the mighty and the people of the holy ones.[^25]
וְעָצַ֤ם כֹּחוֹ֙ וְלֹ֣א בְכֹח֔וֹ וְנִפְלָא֥וֹת יַשְׁחִ֖ית וְהִצְלִ֣יחַ וְעָשָׂ֑ה וְהִשְׁחִ֥ית עֲצוּמִ֖ים וְעַם־קְדֹשִֽׁים׃

By his cunning he will make deceit succeed under his hand, and in his heart he will make himself great. Without warning[^26] he will destroy many. He will even stand up against the Prince of princes, but he will be broken, and not by human hand.[^27]
וְעַל־שִׂכְל֗וֹ וְהִצְלִ֤יחַ מִרְמָה֙ בְּיָד֔וֹ וּבִלְבָב֣וֹ יַגְדִּ֔יל וּבְשַׁלְוָ֖ה יַשְׁחִ֣ית רַבִּ֑ים וְעַ֤ל שַׂר־שָׂרִים֙ יַעֲמֹ֔ד וּבְאֶ֥פֶס יָ֖ד יִשָּׁבֵֽר׃
The vision of the evenings and the mornings that has been told is true. But you, keep the vision secret,[^28] for it refers to many days from now."
וּמַרְאֵ֨ה הָעֶ֧רֶב וְהַבֹּ֛קֶר אֲשֶׁ֥ר נֶאֱמַ֖ר אֱמֶ֣ת ה֑וּא וְאַתָּה֙ סְתֹ֣ם הֶֽחָז֔וֹן כִּ֖י לְיָמִ֥ים רַבִּֽים׃
And I, Daniel, was overcome[^29] and lay sick for some days. Then I got up and went about the king's business. But I was appalled by the vision, and no one could explain it.[^30]
וַאֲנִ֣י דָנִיֵּ֗אל נִהְיֵ֤יתִי וְנֽ͏ֶחֱלֵ֙יתִי֙ יָמִ֔ים וָאָק֕וּם וָאֶֽעֱשֶׂ֖ה אֶת־מְלֶ֣אכֶת הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וָאֶשְׁתּוֹמֵ֥ם עַל־הַמַּרְאֶ֖ה וְאֵ֥ין מֵבִֽין׃ פ

n.1: From here to the end of the book the text is in Hebrew again. The Aramaic section, 2:4–7:28, has ended.
n.2: Or "in Susa the citadel". Susa was later one of the royal cities of the Persian kings (Nehemiah 1:1; Esther 1:2).
n.3: Hebrew *uval*, probably "canal" or "watercourse"; the Septuagint and the Vulgate understood "gate". The Ulai flowed past Susa. Also in verses 3 and 6.
n.4: Literally "a horn from smallness". This horn is probably Antiochus IV Epiphanes (175–164 BC), king of the Seleucid empire, one of the kingdoms that came from the empire of Alexander the Great (verses 21–22). In 167 BC he stopped the sacrifices in the temple in Jerusalem (1 Maccabees 1:20–64). Compare 7:8, 25; 11:21–45.
n.5: Hebrew *ha-tsevi*, "the beauty, the glory", here the land of Israel (compare 11:16, 41; Jeremiah 3:19; Ezekiel 20:6).
n.6: Hebrew *sar ha-tsava*, "the prince of the host": God himself, or an angelic commander of his armies (compare Joshua 5:14–15).
n.7: The Hebrew text is written "It took the regular offering away from him" but read "The regular offering was taken away from him". *Ha-tamid*, "the continual", is the regular burnt offering made every morning and evening (Exodus 29:38–42; Numbers 28:3–8). Also in verses 12–13.
n.8: The Hebrew of this verse is difficult. It may also mean "A host was set over the regular offering in transgression".
n.9: Hebrew *palmoni*, "a certain one", used of someone whose name is not given.
n.10: Hebrew *ha-pesha shomem*. Compare "the abomination that causes desolation" in 9:27; 11:31 and 12:11.
n.11: The Septuagint and Theodotion read "to him".
n.12: Literally "evening morning": either 2,300 days, or 2,300 evening and morning offerings, that is, 1,150 days.
n.13: Literally "will be put right" or "will be vindicated". The temple was cleansed and rededicated in December 164 BC (1 Maccabees 4:36–59), the origin of the festival of Hanukkah.
n.14: Hebrew *gever*, "a man", which sounds like the first part of the name Gabriel in verse 16.
n.15: Gabriel means "man of God" or "God is mighty". With Michael (10:13, 21; 12:1), he is one of the only two angels named in the Hebrew Bible. Compare Luke 1:19, 26.
n.16: Hebrew *ben adam*, "a human being, a mortal", the title by which God addresses Ezekiel. Compare 7:13.
n.17: Literally "made me stand where I stood".
n.18: Hebrew *za'am*, God's anger against his people (compare Isaiah 10:5, 25).
n.19: Or "for the end will come at the appointed time".
n.21: Alexander the Great, who conquered the Persian Empire between 334 and 330 BC and died in 323 BC.
n.22: After Alexander's death his empire was divided among his generals. Among the kingdoms that came from it were the Ptolemaic kingdom in Egypt and the Seleucid kingdom in Syria and Mesopotamia.
n.23: Literally "strong of face and understanding riddles".
n.26: Or "When they feel secure". Literally "in ease".
n.27: Literally "and without a hand". Antiochus IV died of illness in 164 BC while on campaign in Persia (1 Maccabees 6:1–16).
n.29: Literally "was finished". The meaning of the Hebrew *nihyeti* is uncertain.
n.30: Or "and I did not understand it". Literally "and there was no one who understood".

v: In the first year of Darius son of Ahasuerus, a Mede by descent,[^1] who was made king over the kingdom of the Babylonians,[^2]
בִּשְׁנַ֣ת אַחַ֗ת לְדָרְיָ֛וֶשׁ בֶּן־אֲחַשְׁוֵר֖וֹשׁ מִזֶּ֣רַע מָדָ֑י אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָמְלַ֔ךְ עַ֖ל מַלְכ֥וּת כַּשְׂדִּֽים׃

in the first year of his reign, I, Daniel, understood from the books the number of years that, according to the word of the LORD[^3] to Jeremiah the prophet, must pass until the desolation of Jerusalem came to an end: seventy years.[^4]

בִּשְׁנַ֤ת אַחַת֙ לְמָלְכ֔וֹ אֲנִי֙ דָּֽנִיֵּ֔אל בִּינֹ֖תִי בַּסְּפָרִ֑ים מִסְפַּ֣ר הַשָּׁנִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר הָיָ֤ה דְבַר־יְהוָה֙ אֶל־יִרְמִיָ֣ה הַנָּבִ֔יא לְמַלֹּ֛אות לְחָרְב֥וֹת יְרוּשָׁלַ֖͏ִם שִׁבְעִ֥ים שָׁנָֽה׃
So I turned my face to the Lord God,[^5] to seek him by prayer and pleas for mercy, with fasting, sackcloth and ashes.
וָאֶתְּנָ֣ה אֶת־פָּנַ֗י אֶל־אֲדֹנָי֙ הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים לְבַקֵּ֥שׁ תְּפִלָּ֖ה וְתַחֲנוּנִ֑ים בְּצ֖וֹם וְשַׂ֥ק וָאֵֽפֶר׃
I prayed to the LORD my God and made confession. I said, "Ah, Lord, the great and awesome God, who keeps covenant and faithful love with those who love him and keep his commands,[^6]
וָֽאֶתְפַּֽלְלָ֛ה לַיהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהַ֖י וָאֶתְוַדֶּ֑ה וָאֹֽמְרָ֗ה אָנָּ֤א אֲדֹנָי֙ הָאֵ֤ל הַגָּדוֹל֙ וְהַנּוֹרָ֔א שֹׁמֵ֤ר הַבְּרִית֙ וְֽהַחֶ֔סֶד לְאֹהֲבָ֖יו וּלְשֹׁמְרֵ֥י מִצְוֺתָֽיו׃
we have sinned and done wrong. We have acted wickedly and rebelled, turning away from your commands and your rulings.
חָטָ֥אנוּ וְעָוִ֖ינוּ *והרשענו **הִרְשַׁ֣עְנוּ וּמָרָ֑דְנוּ וְס֥וֹר מִמִּצְוֺתֶ֖ךָ וּמִמִּשְׁפָּטֶֽיךָ׃
We have not listened to your servants the prophets, who spoke in your name to our kings, our officials and our ancestors, and to all the people of the land.
וְלֹ֤א שָׁמַ֙עְנוּ֙ אֶל־עֲבָדֶ֣יךָ הַנְּבִיאִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר דִּבְּרוּ֙ בְּשִׁמְךָ֔ אֶל־מְלָכֵ֥ינוּ שָׂרֵ֖ינוּ וַאֲבֹתֵ֑ינוּ וְאֶ֖ל כָּל־עַ֥ם הָאָֽרֶץ׃

To you, Lord, belongs righteousness, but to us open shame,[^7] as it is this day: to the people of Judah, to those who live in Jerusalem, and to all Israel, those near and those far away, in all the lands to which you have driven them because of the unfaithfulness they have committed against you.

לְךָ֤ אֲדֹנָי֙ הַצְּדָקָ֔ה וְלָ֛נוּ בֹּ֥שֶׁת הַפָּנִ֖ים כַּיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה לְאִ֤ישׁ יְהוּדָה֙ וּלְיוֹשְׁבֵ֣י יְרֽוּשָׁלִַ֔ם וּֽלְכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֞ל הַקְּרֹבִ֣ים וְהָרְחֹקִ֗ים בְּכָל־הָֽאֲרָצוֹת֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הִדַּחְתָּ֣ם שָׁ֔ם בְּמַעֲלָ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר מָֽעֲלוּ־בָֽךְ׃
LORD, to us belongs open shame: to our kings, our officials and our ancestors, because we have sinned against you.
יְהוָ֗ה לָ֚נוּ בֹּ֣שֶׁת הַפָּנִ֔ים לִמְלָכֵ֥ינוּ לְשָׂרֵ֖ינוּ וְלַאֲבֹתֵ֑ינוּ אֲשֶׁ֥ר חָטָ֖אנוּ לָֽךְ׃
To the Lord our God belong compassion and forgiveness, though we have rebelled against him.[^8]
לַֽאדֹנָ֣י אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ הָרַחֲמִ֖ים וְהַסְּלִח֑וֹת כִּ֥י מָרַ֖דְנוּ בּֽוֹ׃
We have not obeyed the voice of the LORD our God by living according to his instructions,[^9] which he set before us through his servants the prophets.
וְלֹ֣א שָׁמַ֔עְנוּ בְּק֖וֹל יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֑ינוּ לָלֶ֤כֶת בְּתֽוֹרֹתָיו֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נָתַ֣ן לְפָנֵ֔ינוּ בְּיַ֖ד עֲבָדָ֥יו הַנְּבִיאִֽים׃

All Israel has broken your law and turned away, refusing to obey your voice. So the curse and the oath written in the Law of Moses, the servant of God, have been poured out on us, because we have sinned against him.[^10]

וְכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל עָֽבְרוּ֙ אֶת־תּ֣וֹרָתֶ֔ךָ וְס֕וֹר לְבִלְתִּ֖י שְׁמ֣וֹעַ בְּקֹלֶ֑ךָ וַתִּתַּ֨ךְ עָלֵ֜ינוּ הָאָלָ֣ה וְהַשְּׁבֻעָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר כְּתוּבָה֙ בְּתוֹרַת֙ מֹשֶׁ֣ה עֶֽבֶד־הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים כִּ֥י חָטָ֖אנוּ לֽוֹ׃

He has carried out his word[^11] that he spoke against us and against our rulers who ruled us,[^12] by bringing on us a great disaster. Under the whole heaven nothing has ever been done like what has been done to Jerusalem.

וַיָּ֜קֶם אֶת־*דבריו **דְּבָר֣וֹ ׀ אֲשֶׁר־דִּבֶּ֣ר עָלֵ֗ינוּ וְעַ֤ל שֹֽׁפְטֵ֙ינוּ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר שְׁפָט֔וּנוּ לְהָבִ֥יא עָלֵ֖ינוּ רָעָ֣ה גְדֹלָ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹֽא־נֶעֶשְׂתָ֗ה תַּ֚חַת כָּל־הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר נֶעֶשְׂתָ֖ה בִּירוּשָׁלָֽ͏ִם׃
Just as it is written in the Law of Moses, all this disaster has come on us. Yet we have not sought the favor of the LORD our God[^13] by turning from our iniquities and paying heed to your truth.
כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר כָּתוּב֙ בְּתוֹרַ֣ת מֹשֶׁ֔ה אֵ֛ת כָּל־הָרָעָ֥ה הַזֹּ֖את בָּ֣אָה עָלֵ֑ינוּ וְלֹֽא־חִלִּ֜ינוּ אֶת־פְּנֵ֣י ׀ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֗ינוּ לָשׁוּב֙ מֵֽעֲוֺנֵ֔נוּ וּלְהַשְׂכִּ֖יל בַּאֲמִתֶּֽךָ׃
So the LORD kept watch over the disaster and brought it on us, for the LORD our God is righteous in all the works he has done, and we have not obeyed his voice.
וַיִּשְׁקֹ֤ד יְהוָה֙ עַל־הָ֣רָעָ֔ה וַיְבִיאֶ֖הָ עָלֵ֑ינוּ כִּֽי־צַדִּ֞יק יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֗ינוּ עַל־כָּל־מַֽעֲשָׂיו֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֔ה וְלֹ֥א שָׁמַ֖עְנוּ בְּקֹלֽוֹ׃
And now, Lord our God, who brought your people out of the land of Egypt with a mighty hand and made a name for yourself, as it is this day, we have sinned, we have acted wickedly.
וְעַתָּ֣ה ׀ אֲדֹנָ֣י אֱלֹהֵ֗ינוּ אֲשֶׁר֩ הוֹצֵ֨אתָ אֶֽת־עַמְּךָ֜ מֵאֶ֤רֶץ מִצְרַ֙יִם֙ בְּיָ֣ד חֲזָקָ֔ה וַתַּֽעַשׂ־לְךָ֥ שֵׁ֖ם כַּיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה חָטָ֖אנוּ רָשָֽׁעְנוּ׃

Lord, in keeping with all your righteous acts, let your anger and your wrath turn away from your city Jerusalem, your holy mountain. Because of our sins and the iniquities of our ancestors, Jerusalem and your people have become a disgrace to all who are around us.

אֲדֹנָ֗י כְּכָל־צִדְקֹתֶ֙ךָ֙ יָֽשָׁב־נָ֤א אַפְּךָ֙ וַחֲמָ֣תְךָ֔ מֵעִֽירְךָ֥ יְרוּשָׁלַ֖͏ִם הַר־קָדְשֶׁ֑ךָ כִּ֤י בַחֲטָאֵ֙ינוּ֙ וּבַעֲוֺנ֣וֹת אֲבֹתֵ֔ינוּ יְרוּשָׁלַ֧͏ִם וְעַמְּךָ֛ לְחֶרְפָּ֖ה לְכָל־סְבִיבֹתֵֽינוּ׃
Now, our God, listen to the prayer of your servant and to his pleas for mercy. For the Lord's sake,[^14] make your face shine on your desolate sanctuary.
וְעַתָּ֣ה ׀ שְׁמַ֣ע אֱלֹהֵ֗ינוּ אֶל־תְּפִלַּ֤ת עַבְדְּךָ֙ וְאֶל־תַּ֣חֲנוּנָ֔יו וְהָאֵ֣ר פָּנֶ֔יךָ עַל־מִקְדָּשְׁךָ֖ הַשָּׁמֵ֑ם לְמַ֖עַן אֲדֹנָֽי׃

Turn your ear, my God, and hear. Open your eyes and see our desolations and the city that is called by your name.[^15] We do not lay our pleas before you because of our righteous acts, but because of your great compassion.

הַטֵּ֨ה אֱלֹהַ֥י ׀ אָזְנְךָ֮ וּֽשֲׁמָע֒ *פקחה **פְּקַ֣ח עֵינֶ֗יךָ וּרְאֵה֙ שֹֽׁמְמֹתֵ֔ינוּ וְהָעִ֕יר אֲשֶׁר־נִקְרָ֥א שִׁמְךָ֖ עָלֶ֑יהָ כִּ֣י ׀ לֹ֣א עַל־צִדְקֹתֵ֗ינוּ אֲנַ֨חְנוּ מַפִּילִ֤ים תַּחֲנוּנֵ֙ינוּ֙ לְפָנֶ֔יךָ כִּ֖י עַל־רַחֲמֶ֥יךָ הָרַבִּֽים׃
Lord, hear! Lord, forgive! Lord, listen and act! Do not delay, for your own sake, my God, for your city and your people are called by your name."
אֲדֹנָ֤י ׀ שְׁמָ֙עָה֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י ׀ סְלָ֔חָה אֲדֹנָ֛י הַֽקֲשִׁ֥יבָה וַעֲשֵׂ֖ה אַל־תְּאַחַ֑ר לְמַֽעֲנְךָ֣ אֱלֹהַ֔י כִּֽי־שִׁמְךָ֣ נִקְרָ֔א עַל־עִירְךָ֖ וְעַל־עַמֶּֽךָ׃
While I was still speaking and praying, confessing my sin and the sin of my people Israel, and laying my plea before the LORD my God for the holy mountain of my God,
וְע֨וֹד אֲנִ֤י מְדַבֵּר֙ וּמִתְפַּלֵּ֔ל וּמִתְוַדֶּה֙ חַטָּאתִ֔י וְחַטַּ֖את עַמִּ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וּמַפִּ֣יל תְּחִנָּתִ֗י לִפְנֵי֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהַ֔י עַ֖ל הַר־קֹ֥דֶשׁ אֱלֹהָֽי׃
while I was still speaking in prayer, the man Gabriel, whom I had seen in the vision at the first, came to me in swift flight[^16] at about the time of the evening offering.[^17]
וְע֛וֹד אֲנִ֥י מְדַבֵּ֖ר בַּתְּפִלָּ֑ה וְהָאִ֣ישׁ גַּבְרִיאֵ֡ל אֲשֶׁר֩ רָאִ֨יתִי בֶחָז֤וֹן בַּתְּחִלָּה֙ מֻעָ֣ף בִּיעָ֔ף נֹגֵ֣עַ אֵלַ֔י כְּעֵ֖ת מִנְחַת־עָֽרֶב׃
He gave me understanding[^18] and spoke with me. He said, "Daniel, I have now come out to give you insight and understanding.
וַיָּ֖בֶן וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר עִמִּ֑י וַיֹּאמַ֕ר דָּנִיֵּ֕אל עַתָּ֥ה יָצָ֖אתִי לְהַשְׂכִּילְךָ֥ בִינָֽה׃
At the beginning of your pleas for mercy a word went out, and I have come to tell it to you, for you are greatly loved.[^19] So consider the word and understand the vision.
בִּתְחִלַּ֨ת תַּחֲנוּנֶ֜יךָ יָצָ֣א דָבָ֗ר וַאֲנִי֙ בָּ֣אתִי לְהַגִּ֔יד כִּ֥י חֲמוּד֖וֹת אָ֑תָּה וּבִין֙ בַּדָּבָ֔ר וְהָבֵ֖ן בַּמַּרְאֶֽה׃

Seventy weeks[^20] are decreed for your people and your holy city, to finish the transgression, to put an end to sin,[^21] to atone for iniquity, to bring in everlasting righteousness, to seal up vision and prophet, and to anoint a most holy place.[^22]

שָׁבֻעִ֨ים שִׁבְעִ֜ים נֶחְתַּ֥ךְ עַֽל־עַמְּךָ֣ ׀ וְעַל־עִ֣יר קָדְשֶׁ֗ךָ לְכַלֵּ֨א הַפֶּ֜שַׁע *ולחתם **וּלְהָתֵ֤ם *חטאות **חַטָּאת֙ וּלְכַפֵּ֣ר עָוֺ֔ן וּלְהָבִ֖יא צֶ֣דֶק עֹֽלָמִ֑ים וְלַחְתֹּם֙ חָז֣וֹן וְנָבִ֔יא וְלִמְשֹׁ֖חַ קֹ֥דֶשׁ קָֽדָשִֽׁים׃

Know and understand this: from the going out of the word to restore and rebuild Jerusalem until an anointed one, a ruler,[^23] there will be seven weeks. Then for sixty-two weeks it will be built again, with square and moat,[^24] but in troubled times.[^25]

וְתֵדַ֨ע וְתַשְׂכֵּ֜ל מִן־מֹצָ֣א דָבָ֗ר לְהָשִׁיב֙ וְלִבְנ֤וֹת יְרֽוּשָׁלִַ֙ם֙ עַד־מָשִׁ֣יחַ נָגִ֔יד שָׁבֻעִ֖ים שִׁבְעָ֑ה וְשָׁבֻעִ֞ים שִׁשִּׁ֣ים וּשְׁנַ֗יִם תָּשׁוּב֙ וְנִבְנְתָה֙ רְח֣וֹב וְחָר֔וּץ וּבְצ֖וֹק הָעִתִּֽים׃

After the sixty-two weeks, an anointed one will be cut off and will have nothing.[^26] The people of a ruler who is to come will destroy the city and the sanctuary. Its end will come with a flood,[^27] and to the end there will be war. Desolations are decreed.

וְאַחֲרֵ֤י הַשָּׁבֻעִים֙ שִׁשִּׁ֣ים וּשְׁנַ֔יִם יִכָּרֵ֥ת מָשִׁ֖יחַ וְאֵ֣ין ל֑וֹ וְהָעִ֨יר וְהַקֹּ֜דֶשׁ יַ֠שְׁחִית עַ֣ם נָגִ֤יד הַבָּא֙ וְקִצּ֣וֹ בַשֶּׁ֔טֶף וְעַד֙ קֵ֣ץ מִלְחָמָ֔ה נֶחֱרֶ֖צֶת שֹׁמֵמֽוֹת׃

He will make a firm covenant with many[^28] for one week, and for half of the week he will put a stop to sacrifice and offering. And on a wing of abominations will come one who makes desolate,[^29] until the end that is decreed is poured out on the one who makes desolate."
וְהִגְבִּ֥יר בְּרִ֛ית לָרַבִּ֖ים שָׁב֣וּעַ אֶחָ֑ד וַחֲצִ֨י הַשָּׁב֜וּעַ יַשְׁבִּ֣ית ׀ זֶ֣בַח וּמִנְחָ֗ה וְעַ֨ל כְּנַ֤ף שִׁקּוּצִים֙ מְשֹׁמֵ֔ם וְעַד־כָּלָה֙ וְנֶ֣חֱרָצָ֔ה תִּתַּ֖ךְ עַל־שֹׁמֵֽם׃ פ

n.1: Literally "from the seed of Media". On Darius the Mede, see 6:1.
n.3: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles. This chapter is the only place in Daniel where the name is used.
n.5: Hebrew *Adonai ha-Elohim*. *Adonai*, "the Lord", is also used in verses 4, 7, 9, 15–17 and 19.
n.6: Compare Deuteronomy 7:9; Nehemiah 1:5. *Faithful love* is Hebrew *chesed*, loyal, covenant love.
n.7: Literally "shame of face". Also in verse 8.
n.8: Or "for we have rebelled against him".
n.10: See Leviticus 26:14–39; Deuteronomy 28:15–68; 29:19–20 (29:20–21 in most English Bibles).
n.11: The Hebrew text is written "his words" but read "his word".
n.13: Literally "we have not softened the face of the LORD our God".
n.14: Literally "For the sake of the Lord". Theodotion reads "For your own sake, Lord".
n.15: Literally "over which your name is called". Also in verse 19.
n.16: Or "when I was completely weary". The meaning of the Hebrew *mu'af bi'af* is uncertain: it may come from a word meaning "to fly" or from one meaning "to be weary".
n.17: Hebrew *minchat erev*, offered in the late afternoon (1 Kings 18:36; Ezra 9:4–5).
n.18: The Septuagint and Theodotion read "He came", a reading that differs from the Hebrew by one letter.
n.19: Literally "you are precious things". Also in 10:11, 19.
n.20: Hebrew *shavu'im shiv'im*, "seventy sevens": seventy periods of seven, usually understood as weeks of years, 490 years in all (compare Leviticus 25:8). The seventy years of Jeremiah's prophecy (verse 2) become seventy times seven years. Also in verses 25–27.
n.21: The Hebrew text is written "to seal up sins" but read "to put an end to sin".
n.22: Or "a most holy one". Hebrew *qodesh qodashim*, "holy of holies", which elsewhere means the most holy place in the tabernacle and temple (Exodus 26:33–34) or the most holy things of the sanctuary (Exodus 29:37; 30:29). Some ancient and later interpreters understood it of a person.
n.23: Hebrew *mashiach nagid*, "an anointed one, a ruler" or "an anointed ruler". *Mashiach* means one anointed with oil, as kings and priests were. Interpreters who follow the Masoretic accents (see the next note) have identified this figure with Cyrus, whom Isaiah 45:1 calls the LORD's anointed, or with Zerubbabel or the high priest Joshua after the exile (Ezra 3:2). Christian tradition read here the coming of the Messiah, Jesus: "unto the Messiah the Prince" (King James Version).
n.24: Hebrew *rechov ve-charuts*, "open square and moat". *Charuts* may also mean "decreed".
n.25: The translation follows the Masoretic accents, which separate the seven weeks from the sixty-two weeks. The Vulgate and older English translations such as the King James Version join them: "there will be seven weeks and sixty-two weeks; the street will be built again".
n.26: Literally "and there will not be to him". The meaning is uncertain: perhaps "and will have no one" or "and will be no more". Many modern interpreters identify this anointed one with the high priest Onias III, who was murdered in about 171 BC (2 Maccabees 4:33–35), and the coming ruler with Antiochus IV (see 8:9). Christian tradition has understood the verse of the death of Jesus and the destruction of Jerusalem by the Romans in AD 70.
n.27: Or "His end will come in a flood", referring to the ruler.
n.28: Hebrew *la-rabbim*, "with the many", a phrase that recurs in 11:33, 39; 12:3. *He* is probably the coming ruler of verse 26.
n.29: The Hebrew is difficult. "Wing" may mean a corner or a high point of the temple or its altar. *Shiqqutsim meshomem*, "abominations that make desolate", is echoed in 11:31 and 12:11 ("the abomination that causes desolation"), probably a pagan altar or image set up in the temple in 167 BC (1 Maccabees 1:54). The phrase is taken up in Mark 13:14 and Matthew 24:15.

v: In the third year of Cyrus king of Persia,[^1] a word was revealed to Daniel, who was called Belteshazzar. The word was true, and it concerned a great conflict.[^2] He understood the word and had understanding of the vision.

בִּשְׁנַ֣ת שָׁל֗וֹשׁ לְכ֙וֹרֶשׁ֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ פָּרַ֔ס דָּבָר֙ נִגְלָ֣ה לְדָֽנִיֵּ֔אל אֲשֶׁר־נִקְרָ֥א שְׁמ֖וֹ בֵּלְטְשַׁאצַּ֑ר וֶאֱמֶ֤ת הַדָּבָר֙ וְצָבָ֣א גָד֔וֹל וּבִין֙ אֶת־הַדָּבָ֔ר וּבִ֥ינָה ל֖וֹ בַּמַּרְאֶֽה׃
At that time I, Daniel, had been mourning for three whole weeks.[^3]
בַּיָּמִ֖ים הָהֵ֑ם אֲנִ֤י דָֽנִיֵּאל֙ הָיִ֣יתִי מִתְאַבֵּ֔ל שְׁלֹשָׁ֥ה שָׁבֻעִ֖ים יָמִֽים׃
I ate no rich food,[^4] no meat or wine entered my mouth, and I did not anoint myself at all until the three whole weeks were over.
לֶ֣חֶם חֲמֻד֞וֹת לֹ֣א אָכַ֗לְתִּי וּבָשָׂ֥ר וָיַ֛יִן לֹא־בָ֥א אֶל־פִּ֖י וְס֣וֹךְ לֹא־סָ֑כְתִּי עַד־מְלֹ֕את שְׁלֹ֥שֶׁת שָׁבֻעִ֖ים יָמִֽים׃ פ
On the twenty-fourth day of the first month,[^5] I was on the bank of the great river, the Tigris.[^6]
וּבְי֛וֹם עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וְאַרְבָּעָ֖ה לַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הָרִאשׁ֑וֹן וַאֲנִ֗י הָיִ֛יתִי עַ֣ל יַ֧ד הַנָּהָ֛ר הַגָּד֖וֹל ה֥וּא חִדָּֽקֶל׃
I lifted my eyes and looked, and there was a man dressed in linen, with a belt of fine gold from Uphaz[^7] around his waist.
וָאֶשָּׂ֤א אֶת־עֵינַי֙ וָאֵ֔רֶא וְהִנֵּ֥ה אִישׁ־אֶחָ֖ד לָב֣וּשׁ בַּדִּ֑ים וּמָתְנָ֥יו חֲגֻרִ֖ים בְּכֶ֥תֶם אוּפָֽז׃

His body was like beryl,[^8] his face like the appearance of lightning, his eyes like flaming torches, his arms and his legs like the gleam of polished bronze, and the sound of his words like the sound of a multitude.[^9]
וּגְוִיָּת֣וֹ כְתַרְשִׁ֗ישׁ וּפָנָ֞יו כְּמַרְאֵ֤ה בָרָק֙ וְעֵינָיו֙ כְּלַפִּ֣ידֵי אֵ֔שׁ וּזְרֹֽעֹתָיו֙ וּמַרְגְּלֹתָ֔יו כְּעֵ֖ין נְחֹ֣שֶׁת קָלָ֑ל וְק֥וֹל דְּבָרָ֖יו כְּק֥וֹל הָמֽוֹן׃
I, Daniel, was the only one who saw the vision. The men who were with me did not see the vision, but great terror fell on them, and they fled and hid themselves.
וְרָאִיתִי֩ אֲנִ֨י דָנִיֵּ֤אל לְבַדִּי֙ אֶת־הַמַּרְאָ֔ה וְהָאֲנָשִׁים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָי֣וּ עִמִּ֔י לֹ֥א רָא֖וּ אֶת־הַמַּרְאָ֑ה אֲבָ֗ל חֲרָדָ֤ה גְדֹלָה֙ נָפְלָ֣ה עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם וַֽיִּבְרְח֖וּ בְּהֵחָבֵֽא׃
So I was left alone, and I saw this great vision. No strength was left in me. My face turned deathly pale,[^10] and I retained no strength.
וַאֲנִי֙ נִשְׁאַ֣רְתִּי לְבַדִּ֔י וָֽאֶרְאֶ֗ה אֶת־הַמַּרְאָ֤ה הַגְּדֹלָה֙ הַזֹּ֔את וְלֹ֥א נִשְׁאַר־בִּ֖י כֹּ֑ח וְהוֹדִ֗י נֶהְפַּ֤ךְ עָלַי֙ לְמַשְׁחִ֔ית וְלֹ֥א עָצַ֖רְתִּי כֹּֽחַ׃
Then I heard the sound of his words, and as I heard the sound of his words, I fell into a deep sleep on my face, with my face to the ground.
וָאֶשְׁמַ֖ע אֶת־ק֣וֹל דְּבָרָ֑יו וּכְשָׁמְעִי֙ אֶת־ק֣וֹל דְּבָרָ֔יו וַאֲנִ֗י הָיִ֛יתִי נִרְדָּ֥ם עַל־פָּנַ֖י וּפָנַ֥י אָֽרְצָה׃
Then a hand touched me and set me trembling on my knees and the palms of my hands.
וְהִנֵּה־יָ֖ד נָ֣גְעָה בִּ֑י וַתְּנִיעֵ֥נִי עַל־בִּרְכַּ֖י וְכַפּ֥וֹת יָדָֽי׃

He said to me, "Daniel, greatly loved man,[^11] understand the words that I am speaking to you, and stand up where you are,[^12] for I have now been sent to you." When he had spoken this word to me, I stood up trembling.

וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֡י דָּנִיֵּ֣אל אִישׁ־חֲ֠מֻדוֹת הָבֵ֨ן בַּדְּבָרִ֜ים אֲשֶׁר֩ אָנֹכִ֨י דֹבֵ֤ר אֵלֶ֙יךָ֙ וַעֲמֹ֣ד עַל־עָמְדֶ֔ךָ כִּ֥י עַתָּ֖ה שֻׁלַּ֣חְתִּי אֵלֶ֑יךָ וּבְדַבְּר֥וֹ עִמִּ֛י אֶת־הַדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּ֖ה עָמַ֥דְתִּי מַרְעִֽיד׃

Then he said to me, "Do not be afraid, Daniel, for from the first day that you set your heart to understand and to humble yourself before your God, your words have been heard, and I have come because of your words.

וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַי֮ אַל־תִּירָ֣א דָנִיֵּאל֒ כִּ֣י ׀ מִן־הַיּ֣וֹם הָרִאשׁ֗וֹן אֲשֶׁ֨ר נָתַ֧תָּ אֶֽת־לִבְּךָ֛ לְהָבִ֧ין וּלְהִתְעַנּ֛וֹת לִפְנֵ֥י אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ נִשְׁמְע֣וּ דְבָרֶ֑יךָ וַאֲנִי־בָ֖אתִי בִּדְבָרֶֽיךָ׃
The prince of the kingdom of Persia[^13] stood against me for twenty-one days. Then Michael,[^14] one of the chief princes, came to help me, and I was left there with the kings of Persia.[^15]
וְשַׂ֣ר ׀ מַלְכ֣וּת פָּרַ֗ס עֹמֵ֤ד לְנֶגְדִּי֙ עֶשְׂרִ֣ים וְאֶחָ֣ד י֔וֹם וְהִנֵּ֣ה מִֽיכָאֵ֗ל אַחַ֛ד הַשָּׂרִ֥ים הָרִאשֹׁנִ֖ים בָּ֣א לְעָזְרֵ֑נִי וַאֲנִי֙ נוֹתַ֣רְתִּי שָׁ֔ם אֵ֖צֶל מַלְכֵ֥י פָרָֽס׃
Now I have come to make you understand what will happen to your people in the last days,[^16] for the vision is for days yet to come."
וּבָ֙אתִי֙ לַהֲבִ֣ינְךָ֔ אֵ֛ת אֲשֶׁר־יִקְרָ֥ה לְעַמְּךָ֖ בְּאַחֲרִ֣ית הַיָּמִ֑ים כִּי־ע֥וֹד חָז֖וֹן לַיָּמִֽים׃
While he was speaking these words with me, I turned my face toward the ground and was speechless.
וּבְדַבְּר֣וֹ עִמִּ֔י כַּדְּבָרִ֖ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה נָתַ֧תִּי פָנַ֛י אַ֖רְצָה וְנֶאֱלָֽמְתִּי׃

Then one who looked like a human being[^17] touched my lips. I opened my mouth and spoke, and I said to the one standing before me, "My lord, because of the vision pains have come over me,[^18] and I retain no strength.

וְהִנֵּ֗ה כִּדְמוּת֙ בְּנֵ֣י אָדָ֔ם נֹגֵ֖עַ עַל־שְׂפָתָ֑י וָאֶפְתַּח־פִּ֗י וָאֲדַבְּרָה֙ וָאֹֽמְרָה֙ אֶל־הָעֹמֵ֣ד לְנֶגְדִּ֔י אֲדֹנִ֗י בַּמַּרְאָה֙ נֶהֶפְכ֤וּ צִירַי֙ עָלַ֔י וְלֹ֥א עָצַ֖רְתִּי כֹּֽחַ׃
How can my lord's servant speak with my lord? As for me, no strength remains in me now, and no breath is left in me."
וְהֵ֣יךְ יוּכַ֗ל עֶ֤בֶד אֲדֹנִי֙ זֶ֔ה לְדַבֵּ֖ר עִם־אֲדֹ֣נִי זֶ֑ה וַאֲנִ֤י מֵעַ֙תָּה֙ לֹֽא־יַעֲמָד־בִּ֣י כֹ֔חַ וּנְשָׁמָ֖ה לֹ֥א נִשְׁאֲרָה־בִֽי׃
Then the one who looked like a human being touched me again and strengthened me.
וַיֹּ֧סֶף וַיִּגַּע־בִּ֛י כְּמַרְאֵ֥ה אָדָ֖ם וַֽיְחַזְּקֵֽנִי׃
He said, "Do not be afraid, greatly loved man. Peace be with you. Be strong, be strong!" As he spoke with me, I was strengthened, and I said, "Let my lord speak, for you have strengthened me."
וַיֹּ֜אמֶר אַל־תִּירָ֧א אִישׁ־חֲמֻד֛וֹת שָׁל֥וֹם לָ֖ךְ חֲזַ֣ק וַחֲזָ֑ק וּֽבְדַבְּר֤וֹ עִמִּי֙ הִתְחַזַּ֔קְתִּי וָאֹֽ[m]מְרָ֛הּ יְדַבֵּ֥ר אֲדֹנִ֖י כִּ֥י חִזַּקְתָּֽנִי׃
Then he said, "Do you know why I have come to you? Now I will go back to fight against the prince of Persia, and when I go out, the prince of Greece will come.
וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הֲיָדַ֙עְתָּ֙ לָמָּה־בָּ֣אתִי אֵלֶ֔יךָ וְעַתָּ֣ה אָשׁ֔וּב לְהִלָּחֵ֖ם עִם־שַׂ֣ר פָּרָ֑ס וַאֲנִ֣י יוֹצֵ֔א וְהִנֵּ֥ה שַׂר־יָוָ֖ן בָּֽא׃
But I will tell you what is written in the book of truth.[^19] There is no one who stands firmly with me against these except Michael, your prince.[^20]
אֲבָל֙ אַגִּ֣יד לְךָ֔ אֶת־הָרָשׁ֥וּם בִּכְתָ֖ב אֱמֶ֑ת וְאֵ֨ין אֶחָ֜ד מִתְחַזֵּ֤ק עִמִּי֙ עַל־אֵ֔לֶּה כִּ֥י אִם־מִיכָאֵ֖ל שַׂרְכֶֽם׃ פ

n.2: Or "a great hardship". Hebrew *tsava gadol*, literally "a great army" or "a great service".
n.3: Literally "three weeks of days". Also in verse 3.
n.5: The month of Nisan, March–April, the month of Passover (Exodus 12:2, 18).
n.7: The location of Uphaz is unknown (Jeremiah 10:9).
n.8: Hebrew *tarshish*, a precious stone, perhaps yellow jasper or topaz (Exodus 28:20; Ezekiel 1:16).
n.10: Literally "my splendor was turned on me to ruin".
n.11: Literally "man of precious things". See 9:23. Also in verse 19.
n.13: An angelic being, the heavenly ruler of Persia. Compare "the prince of Greece" in verse 20.
n.14: Michael means "Who is like God?". He is the angel who protects Israel (verse 21; 12:1). Compare Jude 9 and Revelation 12:7.
n.15: The Septuagint and Theodotion read "and I left him there with the prince of the kingdom of Persia".
n.16: Literally "at the end of the days". See 2:28.
n.17: Literally "like the likeness of the sons of man"; in verse 18, "like the appearance of a man". Compare 7:13.
n.18: Literally "my pangs have turned upon me", the word used for the pains of childbirth (1 Samuel 4:19).
n.19: Or "the true book". Literally "the writing of truth".
n.20: The Hebrew "your" is plural: the prince of Daniel's people (12:1).

v: "And as for me, in the first year of Darius the Mede, I stood up to support and strengthen him.[^1]
וַאֲנִי֙ בִּשְׁנַ֣ת אַחַ֔ת לְדָרְיָ֖וֶשׁ הַמָּדִ֑י עָמְדִ֛י לְמַחֲזִ֥יק וּלְמָע֖וֹז לֽוֹ׃

Now I will tell you the truth. Three more kings will arise in Persia, and the fourth will be far richer than all of them. When he has grown strong through his riches, he will stir up everyone against the kingdom of Greece.[^2]

וְעַתָּ֕ה אֱמֶ֖ת אַגִּ֣יד לָ֑ךְ הִנֵּה־עוֹד֩ שְׁלֹשָׁ֨ה מְלָכִ֜ים עֹמְדִ֣ים לְפָרַ֗ס וְהָֽרְבִיעִי֙ יַעֲשִׁ֤יר עֹֽשֶׁר־גָּדוֹל֙ מִכֹּ֔ל וּכְחֶזְקָת֣וֹ בְעָשְׁר֔וֹ יָעִ֣יר הַכֹּ֔ל אֵ֖ת מַלְכ֥וּת יָוָֽן׃
Then a mighty king will arise, who will rule with great authority and do as he pleases.[^3]
וְעָמַ֖ד מֶ֣לֶךְ גִּבּ֑וֹר וּמָשַׁל֙ מִמְשָׁ֣ל רַ֔ב וְעָשָׂ֖ה כִּרְצוֹנֽוֹ׃

But as soon as he has arisen, his kingdom will be broken and divided toward the four winds of heaven. It will not go to his descendants, nor will it have the power with which he ruled, for his kingdom will be uprooted and given to others besides these.
וּכְעָמְדוֹ֙ תִּשָּׁבֵ֣ר מַלְכוּת֔וֹ וְתֵחָ֕ץ לְאַרְבַּ֖ע רוּח֣וֹת הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם וְלֹ֣א לְאַחֲרִית֗וֹ וְלֹ֤א כְמָשְׁלוֹ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר מָשָׁ֔ל כִּ֤י תִנָּתֵשׁ֙ מַלְכוּת֔וֹ וְלַאֲחֵרִ֖ים מִלְּבַד־אֵֽלֶּה׃
The king of the south will grow strong, but one of his commanders will grow stronger than he and will rule, and his dominion will be a great dominion.[^4]
וְיֶחֱזַ֥ק מֶֽלֶךְ־הַנֶּ֖גֶב וּמִן־שָׂרָ֑יו וְיֶחֱזַ֤ק עָלָיו֙ וּמָשָׁ֔ל מִמְשָׁ֥ל רַ֖ב מֶמְשַׁלְתּֽוֹ׃

After some years they will make an alliance. The daughter of the king of the south will come to the king of the north to make an agreement, but she will not keep her power,[^5] and he and his power[^6] will not last. She will be given up, together with those who brought her, her father[^7] and the one who supported her in those times.[^8]

וּלְקֵ֤ץ שָׁנִים֙ יִתְחַבָּ֔רוּ וּבַ֣ת מֶֽלֶךְ־הַנֶּ֗גֶב תָּבוֹא֙ אֶל־מֶ֣לֶךְ הַצָּפ֔וֹן לַעֲשׂ֖וֹת מֵישָׁרִ֑ים וְלֹֽא־תַעְצֹ֞ר כּ֣וֹחַ הַזְּר֗וֹעַ וְלֹ֤א יַעֲמֹד֙ וּזְרֹע֔וֹ וְתִנָּתֵ֨ן הִ֤יא וּמְבִיאֶ֙יהָ֙ וְהַיֹּ֣לְדָ֔הּ וּמַחֲזִקָ֖הּ בָּעִתִּֽים׃
A shoot from her roots will arise in his place.[^9] He will come against the army and enter the fortress of the king of the north. He will deal with them and prevail.
וְעָמַ֛ד מִנֵּ֥צֶר שָׁרָשֶׁ֖יהָ כַּנּ֑וֹ וְיָבֹ֣א אֶל־הַחַ֗יִל וְיָבֹא֙ בְּמָעוֹז֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ הַצָּפ֔וֹן וְעָשָׂ֥ה בָהֶ֖ם וְהֶחֱזִֽיק׃
He will also carry off to Egypt their gods, with their cast images[^10] and their precious vessels of silver and gold. Then for some years he will keep away from the king of the north.
וְגַ֣ם אֱ‍ֽלֹהֵיהֶ֡ם עִם־נְסִֽכֵיהֶם֩ עִם־כְּלֵ֨י חֶמְדָּתָ֜ם כֶּ֧סֶף וְזָהָ֛ב בַּשְּׁבִ֖י יָבִ֣א מִצְרָ֑יִם וְהוּא֙ שָׁנִ֣ים יַעֲמֹ֔ד מִמֶּ֖לֶךְ הַצָּפֽוֹן׃
Then the king of the north[^11] will come into the realm of the king of the south, but he will return to his own land.
וּבָ֗א בְּמַלְכוּת֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ הַנֶּ֔גֶב וְשָׁ֖ב אֶל־אַדְמָתֽוֹ׃
His sons will prepare for war and assemble a multitude of great forces. One of them will keep coming, overflow and pass through, and again he will wage war as far as his fortress.[^12]
*ובנו **וּבָנָ֣יו יִתְגָּר֗וּ וְאָסְפוּ֙ הֲמוֹן֙ חֲיָלִ֣ים רַבִּ֔ים וּבָ֥א ב֖וֹא וְשָׁטַ֣ף וְעָבָ֑ר וְיָשֹׁ֥ב *ויתגרו **וְיִתְגָּרֶ֖ה עַד־*מעזה **מָעֻזּֽוֹ׃
Then the king of the south will be enraged and go out and fight against him, the king of the north. He will raise a great multitude, but the multitude will be given into his hand.[^13]
וְיִתְמַרְמַר֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ הַנֶּ֔גֶב וְיָצָ֕א וְנִלְחַ֥ם עִמּ֖וֹ עִם־מֶ֣לֶךְ הַצָּפ֑וֹן וְהֶעֱמִיד֙ הָמ֣וֹן רָ֔ב וְנִתַּ֥ן הֶהָמ֖וֹן בְּיָדֽוֹ׃
When the multitude has been carried off, his heart will be lifted up. He will bring down tens of thousands, but he will not prevail.
וְנִשָּׂ֥א הֶהָמ֖וֹן *ירום **וְרָ֣ם לְבָב֑וֹ וְהִפִּ֛יל רִבֹּא֖וֹת וְלֹ֥א יָעֽוֹז׃
For the king of the north will again raise a multitude, greater than the first, and after some years[^14] he will come on with a great army and much equipment.
וְשָׁב֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ הַצָּפ֔וֹן וְהֶעֱמִ֣יד הָמ֔וֹן רַ֖ב מִן־הָרִאשׁ֑וֹן וּלְקֵ֨ץ הָֽעִתִּ֤ים שָׁנִים֙ יָ֣בוֹא ב֔וֹא בְּחַ֥יִל גָּד֖וֹל וּבִרְכ֥וּשׁ רָֽב׃
In those times many will rise up against the king of the south. Violent men from among your own people will lift themselves up to fulfill the vision, but they will stumble.
וּבָעִתִּ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם רַבִּ֥ים יַֽעַמְד֖וּ עַל־מֶ֣לֶךְ הַנֶּ֑גֶב וּבְנֵ֣י ׀ פָּרִיצֵ֣י עַמְּךָ֗ יִֽנַּשְּׂא֛וּ לְהַעֲמִ֥יד חָז֖וֹן וְנִכְשָֽׁלוּ׃
Then the king of the north will come and pile up a siege ramp and capture a fortified city. The forces of the south will not stand, not even his chosen troops, and there will be no strength to stand.
וְיָבֹא֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ הַצָּפ֔וֹן וְיִשְׁפֹּךְ֙ סֽוֹלֲלָ֔ה וְלָכַ֖ד עִ֣יר מִבְצָר֑וֹת וּזְרֹע֤וֹת הַנֶּ֙גֶב֙ לֹ֣א יַעֲמֹ֔דוּ וְעַם֙ מִבְחָרָ֔יו וְאֵ֥ין כֹּ֖חַ לַעֲמֹֽד׃
The one who comes against him will do as he pleases, and no one will stand before him. He will stand in the beautiful land,[^15] and destruction will be in his hand.[^16]
וְיַ֨עַשׂ הַבָּ֤א אֵלָיו֙ כִּרְצוֹנ֔וֹ וְאֵ֥ין עוֹמֵ֖ד לְפָנָ֑יו וְיַעֲמֹ֥ד בְּאֶֽרֶץ־הַצְּבִ֖י וְכָלָ֥ה בְיָדֽוֹ׃

He will set his face to come with the strength of his whole kingdom, and he will make an agreement with him[^17] and carry it out. He will give him a daughter in marriage[^18] in order to destroy the kingdom,[^19] but she will not stand by him or be on his side.
וְיָשֵׂ֣ם ׀ פָּ֠נָיו לָב֞וֹא בְּתֹ֧קֶף כָּל־מַלְכוּת֛וֹ וִישָׁרִ֥ים עִמּ֖וֹ וְעָשָׂ֑ה וּבַ֤ת הַנָּשִׁים֙ יִתֶּן־ל֣וֹ לְהַשְׁחִיתָ֔הּ וְלֹ֥א תַעֲמֹ֖ד וְלֹא־ל֥וֹ תִהְיֶֽה׃
Then he will turn his face to the coastlands and capture many. But a commander will put an end to his insolence; indeed, he will turn his insolence back on him.[^20]
*וישב **וְיָשֵׂ֧ם ׀ פָּנָ֛יו לְאִיִּ֖ים וְלָכַ֣ד רַבִּ֑ים וְהִשְׁבִּ֨ית קָצִ֤ין חֶרְפָּתוֹ֙ ל֔וֹ בִּלְתִּ֥י חֶרְפָּת֖וֹ יָשִׁ֥יב לֽוֹ׃
Then he will turn his face back toward the fortresses of his own land, but he will stumble and fall and be found no more.[^21]
וְיָשֵׁ֣ב פָּנָ֔יו לְמָעוּזֵּ֖י אַרְצ֑וֹ וְנִכְשַׁ֥ל וְנָפַ֖ל וְלֹ֥א יִמָּצֵֽא׃
In his place will arise one who sends an oppressor through the glory of the kingdom.[^22] But within a few days he will be broken, though not in anger or in battle.
וְעָמַ֧ד עַל־כַּנּ֛וֹ מַעֲבִ֥יר נוֹגֵ֖שׂ הֶ֣דֶר מַלְכ֑וּת וּבְיָמִ֤ים אֲחָדִים֙ יִשָּׁבֵ֔ר וְלֹ֥א בְאַפַּ֖יִם וְלֹ֥א בְמִלְחָמָֽה׃
In his place will arise a contemptible person, who has not been given royal majesty. He will come in without warning[^23] and seize the kingdom through intrigue.[^24]
וְעָמַ֤ד עַל־כַּנּוֹ֙ נִבְזֶ֔ה וְלֹא־נָתְנ֥וּ עָלָ֖יו ה֣וֹד מַלְכ֑וּת וּבָ֣א בְשַׁלְוָ֔ה וְהֶחֱזִ֥יק מַלְכ֖וּת בַּחֲלַקְלַקּֽוֹת׃
Overwhelming forces will be swept away before him[^25] and broken, and also a prince of the covenant.[^26]
וּזְרֹע֥וֹת הַשֶּׁ֛טֶף יִשָּׁטְפ֥וּ מִלְּפָנָ֖יו וְיִשָּׁבֵ֑רוּ וְגַ֖ם נְגִ֥יד בְּרִֽית׃
After an alliance is made with him, he will act deceitfully. He will rise to power with only a small nation.
וּמִן־הִֽתְחַבְּר֥וּת אֵלָ֖יו יַעֲשֶׂ֣ה מִרְמָ֑ה וְעָלָ֥ה וְעָצַ֖ם בִּמְעַט־גּֽוֹי׃

Without warning he will come into the richest parts of the province and do what neither his ancestors nor their ancestors had done: he will scatter plunder, spoil and goods among them. He will devise plans against fortresses, but only for a time.

בְּשַׁלְוָ֞ה וּבְמִשְׁמַנֵּ֣י מְדִינָה֮ יָבוֹא֒ וְעָשָׂ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר לֹא־עָשׂ֤וּ אֲבֹתָיו֙ וַאֲב֣וֹת אֲבֹתָ֔יו בִּזָּ֧ה וְשָׁלָ֛ל וּרְכ֖וּשׁ לָהֶ֣ם יִבְז֑וֹר וְעַ֧ל מִבְצָרִ֛ים יְחַשֵּׁ֥ב מַחְשְׁבֹתָ֖יו וְעַד־עֵֽת׃

He will stir up his strength and his courage against the king of the south with a great army, and the king of the south will wage war with a very great and powerful army, but he will not stand, because of the plots devised against him.[^27]

וְיָעֵר֩ כֹּח֨וֹ וּלְבָב֜וֹ עַל־מֶ֣לֶךְ הַנֶּגֶב֮ בְּחַ֣יִל גָּדוֹל֒ וּמֶ֣לֶךְ הַנֶּ֗גֶב יִתְגָּרֶה֙ לַמִּלְחָמָ֔ה בְּחַֽיִל־גָּד֥וֹל וְעָצ֖וּם עַד־מְאֹ֑ד וְלֹ֣א יַעֲמֹ֔ד כִּֽי־יַחְשְׁב֥וּ עָלָ֖יו מַחֲשָׁבֽוֹת׃
Those who eat his food[^28] will destroy him. His army will be swept away,[^29] and many will fall slain.
וְאֹכְלֵ֧י פַת־בָּג֛וֹ יִשְׁבְּר֖וּהוּ וְחֵיל֣וֹ יִשְׁט֑וֹף וְנָפְל֖וּ חֲלָלִ֥ים רַבִּֽים׃
The two kings, their hearts set on evil, will sit at one table and speak lies to each other, but it will not succeed, for the end is still to come at the appointed time.
וּשְׁנֵיהֶ֤ם הַמְּלָכִים֙ לְבָבָ֣ם לְמֵרָ֔ע וְעַל־שֻׁלְחָ֥ן אֶחָ֖ד כָּזָ֣ב יְדַבֵּ֑רוּ וְלֹ֣א תִצְלָ֔ח כִּי־ע֥וֹד קֵ֖ץ לַמּוֹעֵֽד׃
He will return to his land with great wealth, but his heart will be set against the holy covenant. He will take action and return to his own land.[^30]
וְיָשֹׁ֤ב אַרְצוֹ֙ בִּרְכ֣וּשׁ גָּד֔וֹל וּלְבָב֖וֹ עַל־בְּרִ֣ית קֹ֑דֶשׁ וְעָשָׂ֖ה וְשָׁ֥ב לְאַרְצֽוֹ׃
At the appointed time he will come again into the south, but this time it will not be as it was before.
לַמּוֹעֵ֥ד יָשׁ֖וּב וּבָ֣א בַנֶּ֑גֶב וְלֹֽא־תִהְיֶ֥ה כָרִאשֹׁנָ֖ה וְכָאַחֲרֹנָֽה׃

Ships of Kittim[^31] will come against him, and he will lose heart. He will turn back and rage against the holy covenant and take action. He will return and pay heed to those who abandon the holy covenant.
וּבָ֨אוּ ב֜וֹ צִיִּ֤ים כִּתִּים֙ וְנִכְאָ֔ה וְשָׁ֛ב וְזָעַ֥ם עַל־בְּרִֽית־ק֖וֹדֶשׁ וְעָשָׂ֑ה וְשָׁ֣ב וְיָבֵ֔ן עַל־עֹזְבֵ֖י בְּרִ֥ית קֹֽדֶשׁ׃
Forces sent by him[^32] will rise up and profane the sanctuary, the fortress. They will take away the regular offering[^33] and set up the abomination that causes desolation.[^34]
וּזְרֹעִ֖ים מִמֶּ֣נּוּ יַעֲמֹ֑דוּ וְחִלְּל֞וּ הַמִּקְדָּ֤שׁ הַמָּעוֹז֙ וְהֵסִ֣ירוּ הַתָּמִ֔יד וְנָתְנ֖וּ הַשִּׁקּ֥וּץ מְשׁוֹמֵֽם׃
Those who act wickedly against the covenant he will corrupt with flattery, but the people who know their God will stand firm and take action.
וּמַרְשִׁיעֵ֣י בְרִ֔ית יַחֲנִ֖יף בַּחֲלַקּ֑וֹת וְעַ֛ם יֹדְעֵ֥י אֱלֹהָ֖יו יַחֲזִ֥קוּ וְעָשֽׂוּ׃
Those among the people who are wise[^35] will give understanding to many, though for some days they will fall by sword and flame, by captivity and plunder.
וּמַשְׂכִּ֣ילֵי עָ֔ם יָבִ֖ינוּ לָֽרַבִּ֑ים וְנִכְשְׁל֞וּ בְּחֶ֧רֶב וּבְלֶהָבָ֛ה בִּשְׁבִ֥י וּבְבִזָּ֖ה יָמִֽים׃
When they fall, they will receive a little help,[^36] and many will join them insincerely.
וּבְהִכָּ֣שְׁלָ֔ם יֵעָזְר֖וּ עֵ֣זֶר מְעָ֑ט וְנִלְו֧וּ עֲלֵיהֶ֛ם רַבִּ֖ים בַּחֲלַקְלַקּֽוֹת׃
Some of the wise will fall, so that they may be refined, purified and made white, until the time of the end, for it is still to come at the appointed time.
וּמִן־הַמַּשְׂכִּילִ֣ים יִכָּֽשְׁל֗וּ לִצְר֥וֹף בָּהֶ֛ם וּלְבָרֵ֥ר וְלַלְבֵּ֖ן עַד־עֵ֣ת קֵ֑ץ כִּי־ע֖וֹד לַמּוֹעֵֽד׃

The king will do as he pleases. He will exalt himself and make himself greater than every god, and he will say astonishing things against the God of gods. He will succeed until the wrath is completed, for what has been decreed will be done.
וְעָשָׂ֨ה כִרְצוֹנ֜וֹ הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ וְיִתְרוֹמֵ֤ם וְיִתְגַּדֵּל֙ עַל־כָּל־אֵ֔ל וְעַל֙ אֵ֣ל אֵלִ֔ים יְדַבֵּ֖ר נִפְלָא֑וֹת וְהִצְלִ֙יחַ֙ עַד־כָּ֣לָה זַ֔עַם כִּ֥י נֶחֱרָצָ֖ה נֶעֱשָֽׂתָה׃
He will pay no attention to the gods of his ancestors,[^37] or to the one desired by women,[^38] or to any god, for he will make himself greater than them all.
וְעַל־אֱלֹהֵ֤י אֲבֹתָיו֙ לֹ֣א יָבִ֔ין וְעַל־חֶמְדַּ֥ת נָשִׁ֛ים וְעַֽל־כָּל־אֱל֖וֹהַּ לֹ֣א יָבִ֑ין כִּ֥י עַל־כֹּ֖ל יִתְגַּדָּֽל׃
Instead, he will honor a god of fortresses in their place.[^39] A god whom his ancestors did not know he will honor with gold and silver, with precious stones and costly gifts.
וְלֶאֱלֹ֙הַּ֙ מָֽעֻזִּ֔ים עַל־כַּנּ֖וֹ יְכַבֵּ֑ד וְלֶאֱל֜וֹהַּ אֲשֶׁ֧ר לֹא־יְדָעֻ֣הוּ אֲבֹתָ֗יו יְכַבֵּ֛ד בְּזָהָ֥ב וּבְכֶ֛סֶף וּבְאֶ֥בֶן יְקָרָ֖ה וּבַחֲמֻדֽוֹת׃

He will deal with the strongest fortresses with the help of a foreign god.[^40] Those who acknowledge him he will greatly honor. He will make them rulers over many and distribute land as a reward.[^41]
וְעָשָׂ֞ה לְמִבְצְרֵ֤י מָֽעֻזִּים֙ עִם־אֱל֣וֹהַּ נֵכָ֔ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר *הכיר **יַכִּ֖יר יַרְבֶּ֣ה כָב֑וֹד וְהִמְשִׁילָם֙ בָּֽרַבִּ֔ים וַאֲדָמָ֖ה יְחַלֵּ֥ק בִּמְחִֽיר׃

At the time of the end the king of the south will engage him in battle,[^42] but the king of the north will storm against him with chariots and horsemen and many ships. He will invade countries, overflow and pass through.
וּבְעֵ֣ת קֵ֗ץ יִתְנַגַּ֤ח עִמּוֹ֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ הַנֶּ֔גֶב וְיִשְׂתָּעֵ֨ר עָלָ֜יו מֶ֣לֶךְ הַצָּפ֗וֹן בְּרֶ֙כֶב֙ וּבְפָ֣רָשִׁ֔ים וּבָאֳנִיּ֖וֹת רַבּ֑וֹת וּבָ֥א בַאֲרָצ֖וֹת וְשָׁטַ֥ף וְעָבָֽר׃
He will enter the beautiful land, and many[^43] will fall. But these will escape from his hand: Edom, Moab and the leaders of the Ammonites.[^44]
וּבָא֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ הַצְּבִ֔י וְרַבּ֖וֹת יִכָּשֵׁ֑לוּ וְאֵ֙לֶּה֙ יִמָּלְט֣וּ מִיָּד֔וֹ אֱד֣וֹם וּמוֹאָ֔ב וְרֵאשִׁ֖ית בְּנֵ֥י עַמּֽוֹן׃
He will stretch out his hand against countries, and the land of Egypt will not escape.
וְיִשְׁלַ֥ח יָד֖וֹ בַּאֲרָצ֑וֹת וְאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם לֹ֥א תִהְיֶ֖ה לִפְלֵיטָֽה׃
He will gain control of the treasures of gold and silver and all the precious things of Egypt, and the Libyans and the Cushites[^45] will follow in his steps.
וּמָשַׁ֗ל בְּמִכְמַנֵּי֙ הַזָּהָ֣ב וְהַכֶּ֔סֶף וּבְכֹ֖ל חֲמֻד֣וֹת מִצְרָ֑יִם וְלֻבִ֥ים וְכֻשִׁ֖ים בְּמִצְעָדָֽיו׃
But reports from the east and the north will alarm him, and he will go out in great fury to destroy many and devote them to destruction.[^46]
וּשְׁמֻע֣וֹת יְבַהֲלֻ֔הוּ מִמִּזְרָ֖ח וּמִצָּפ֑וֹן וְיָצָא֙ בְּחֵמָ֣א גְדֹלָ֔ה לְהַשְׁמִ֥יד וּֽלְהַחֲרִ֖ים רַבִּֽים׃
He will pitch his royal tents[^47] between the seas and the beautiful holy mountain.[^48] Yet he will come to his end, and no one will help him.
וְיִטַּע֙ אָהֳלֶ֣י אַפַּדְנ֔וֹ בֵּ֥ין יַמִּ֖ים לְהַר־צְבִי־קֹ֑דֶשׁ וּבָא֙ עַד־קִצּ֔וֹ וְאֵ֥ין עוֹזֵ֖ר לֽוֹ׃

n.1: Probably Michael (10:21). The speech of the man dressed in linen (10:5) continues to 12:4. The kings in this chapter are not named; the notes give the rulers most interpreters identify them with.
n.2: Probably Xerxes I (486–465 BC), who invaded Greece in 480 BC.
n.4: The king of the south is Ptolemy I of Egypt; the commander who became stronger is probably Seleucus I, who founded the Seleucid kingdom of Syria and Mesopotamia, the kingdom of "the king of the north".
n.5: Literally "she will not retain the strength of the arm".
n.6: Or "his offspring", reading the same consonants differently. Literally "his arm".
n.7: Literally "the one who begot her". The same consonants can be read "her child".
n.8: Probably Berenice, daughter of Ptolemy II, who married the Seleucid king Antiochus II in about 252 BC. After his death she and her infant son were murdered.
n.9: Literally "on his base". Probably Berenice's brother Ptolemy III, who invaded the Seleucid kingdom in 246 BC.
n.12: The Hebrew text is written "His son … and they will wage war as far as its fortress" but read "His sons … and he will wage war as far as his fortress". The sons are probably Seleucus III and Antiochus III, who campaigned against Egypt.
n.13: The king of the north will raise a great army, but it will be given into the hand of the king of the south: probably the defeat of Antiochus III by Ptolemy IV at Raphia in 217 BC.
n.14: Literally "at the end of the times, years". Antiochus III returned and defeated Egypt at Panium in about 200 BC, and took control of Judea.
n.16: Or "and all of it will be in his hand".
n.17: Or "he will bring an agreement with him". The meaning of the Hebrew is uncertain.
n.18: Literally "the daughter of women". Probably Cleopatra I, daughter of Antiochus III, who married Ptolemy V in 194/193 BC.
n.19: Literally "to destroy it" or "to destroy her".
n.20: The second half of the verse is difficult in Hebrew. Antiochus III campaigned in Asia Minor and Greece and was defeated by the Romans under Lucius Scipio at Magnesia in 190 BC.
n.21: Antiochus III was killed in 187 BC while plundering a temple in Elymais.
n.22: Or "for the glory of the kingdom", that is, to raise money. Probably Seleucus IV (187–175 BC), whose minister Heliodorus tried to seize the temple treasury in Jerusalem (2 Maccabees 3). "The glory of the kingdom" may be the land of Israel or its temple. Seleucus IV was murdered.
n.23: Literally "in ease". See 8:25. Also in verse 24. The contemptible person is Antiochus IV Epiphanes (175–164 BC), the small horn of 8:9.
n.25: Literally "The arms of the flood will be flooded before him".
n.26: Perhaps the high priest Onias III, who was deposed in 175 BC and murdered in about 171 BC (2 Maccabees 4:7–10, 33–35; compare Daniel 9:26).
n.27: Antiochus IV's first campaign against Egypt and Ptolemy VI, in 170–169 BC.
n.29: Or "His army will sweep everything away".
n.30: On his return from Egypt in 169 BC Antiochus IV plundered the temple in Jerusalem (1 Maccabees 1:20–24).
n.31: Hebrew *Kittim*, the people of Cyprus, later used of other peoples of the west. Here the Romans: in 168 BC a Roman envoy forced Antiochus IV to leave Egypt.
n.34: Hebrew *ha-shiqquts meshomem*. In 167 BC a pagan altar was built on the altar of burnt offering in the temple (1 Maccabees 1:54, 59). Compare 9:27; 12:11; Mark 13:14.
n.35: Hebrew *maskilim*, "those who have insight" or "those who give insight". Also in verse 35 and 12:3, 10.
n.36: Perhaps the revolt led by Judas Maccabeus, which began in 167 BC.
n.38: Probably a god popular among women, such as Tammuz or Adonis (compare Ezekiel 8:14).
n.40: Or "He will man the strongest fortresses with the people of a foreign god", reading the same consonants differently (*am*, "people", for *im*, "with").
n.42: Literally "will butt against him" (compare 8:4). Verses 40–45 do not match what is known of the end of Antiochus IV, who died in Persia in 164 BC (1 Maccabees 6:1–16; see 8:25). Interpreters differ on whether they describe his end in general or symbolic terms, or the end of a ruler still to come.
n.43: Or "many countries". The same consonants can be read "tens of thousands".
n.44: Literally "the first of the sons of Ammon".
n.45: The people of Cush, the region south of Egypt (ancient Nubia).
n.46: Hebrew *le-hacharim*, to devote to God by destroying completely (as in Joshua 6:17–21).
n.47: Hebrew *appeden*, a word borrowed from Persian for a palace or a royal pavilion.
n.48: Literally "the mountain of holy beauty": Mount Zion, where the temple stood. "The seas" may be the Mediterranean.

v: "At that time Michael, the great prince who stands guard over your people,[^1] will arise. There will be a time of distress such as has never been since there was a nation until that time. But at that time your people will be delivered, everyone who is found written in the book.[^2]

וּבָעֵ֣ת הַהִיא֩ יַעֲמֹ֨ד מִֽיכָאֵ֜ל הַשַּׂ֣ר הַגָּד֗וֹל הָעֹמֵד֮ עַל־בְּנֵ֣י עַמֶּךָ֒ וְהָיְתָה֙ עֵ֣ת צָרָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹֽא־נִהְיְתָה֙ מִֽהְי֣וֹת גּ֔וֹי עַ֖ד הָעֵ֣ת הַהִ֑יא וּבָעֵ֤ת הַהִיא֙ יִמָּלֵ֣ט עַמְּךָ֔ כָּל־הַנִּמְצָ֖א כָּת֥וּב בַּסֵּֽפֶר׃
Many of those who sleep in the dust of the earth[^3] will awake, some to everlasting life, and some to disgrace and everlasting contempt.[^4]
וְרַבִּ֕ים מִיְּשֵׁנֵ֥י אַדְמַת־עָפָ֖ר יָקִ֑יצוּ אֵ֚לֶּה לְחַיֵּ֣י עוֹלָ֔ם וְאֵ֥לֶּה לַחֲרָפ֖וֹת לְדִרְא֥וֹן עוֹלָֽם׃ ס
Those who are wise[^5] will shine like the brightness of the sky,[^6] and those who lead many to righteousness will shine like the stars forever and ever.
וְהַ֨מַּשְׂכִּלִ֔ים יַזְהִ֖רוּ כְּזֹ֣הַר הָרָקִ֑יעַ וּמַצְדִּיקֵי֙ הָֽרַבִּ֔ים כַּכּוֹכָבִ֖ים לְעוֹלָ֥ם וָעֶֽד׃ פ
But you, Daniel, keep the words secret and seal the book until the time of the end. Many will run to and fro, and knowledge will increase."[^7]
וְאַתָּ֣ה דָֽנִיֵּ֗אל סְתֹ֧ם הַדְּבָרִ֛ים וַחֲתֹ֥ם הַסֵּ֖פֶר עַד־עֵ֣ת קֵ֑ץ יְשֹׁטְט֥וּ רַבִּ֖ים וְתִרְבֶּ֥ה הַדָּֽעַת׃
Then I, Daniel, looked, and there stood two others, one on this bank of the river and one on that bank of the river.[^8]
וְרָאִ֙יתִי֙ אֲנִ֣י דָנִיֵּ֔אל וְהִנֵּ֛ה שְׁנַ֥יִם אֲחֵרִ֖ים עֹמְדִ֑ים אֶחָ֥ד הֵ֙נָּה֙ לִשְׂפַ֣ת הַיְאֹ֔ר וְאֶחָ֥ד הֵ֖נָּה לִשְׂפַ֥ת הַיְאֹֽר׃
One of them said to the man dressed in linen, who was above the waters of the river, "How long will it be until the end of these wonders?"
וַיֹּ֗אמֶר לָאִישׁ֙ לְב֣וּשׁ הַבַּדִּ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר מִמַּ֖עַל לְמֵימֵ֣י הַיְאֹ֑ר עַד־מָתַ֖י קֵ֥ץ הַפְּלָאֽוֹת׃

I heard the man dressed in linen, who was above the waters of the river. He raised his right hand and his left hand toward heaven and swore by the one who lives forever that it would be for a time, times and half a time,[^9] and that when the shattering of the power of the holy people comes to an end, all these things will be completed.[^10]

וָאֶשְׁמַ֞ע אֶת־הָאִ֣ישׁ ׀ לְב֣וּשׁ הַבַּדִּ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר מִמַּעַל֮ לְמֵימֵ֣י הַיְאֹר֒ וַיָּ֨רֶם יְמִינ֤וֹ וּשְׂמֹאלוֹ֙ אֶל־הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וַיִּשָּׁבַ֖ע בְּחֵ֣י הָעוֹלָ֑ם כִּי֩ לְמוֹעֵ֨ד מֽוֹעֲדִ֜ים וָחֵ֗צִי וּכְכַלּ֛וֹת נַפֵּ֥ץ יַד־עַם־קֹ֖דֶשׁ תִּכְלֶ֥ינָה כָל־אֵֽלֶּה׃
I heard, but I did not understand. So I said, "My lord, what will be the outcome of these things?"
וַאֲנִ֥י שָׁמַ֖עְתִּי וְלֹ֣א אָבִ֑ין וָאֹ֣מְרָ֔ה אֲדֹנִ֕י מָ֥ה אַחֲרִ֖ית אֵֽלֶּה׃ פ
He said, "Go your way, Daniel, for the words are kept secret and sealed until the time of the end.
וַיֹּ֖אמֶר לֵ֣ךְ דָּנִיֵּ֑אל כִּֽי־סְתֻמִ֧ים וַחֲתֻמִ֛ים הַדְּבָרִ֖ים עַד־עֵ֥ת קֵֽץ׃
Many will be purified, made white and refined, but the wicked will act wickedly. None of the wicked will understand, but those who are wise will understand.
יִ֠תְבָּֽרֲרוּ וְיִֽתְלַבְּנ֤וּ וְיִצָּֽרְפוּ֙ רַבִּ֔ים וְהִרְשִׁ֣יעוּ רְשָׁעִ֔ים וְלֹ֥א יָבִ֖ינוּ כָּל־רְשָׁעִ֑ים וְהַמַּשְׂכִּלִ֖ים יָבִֽינוּ׃
From the time that the regular offering[^11] is taken away and the abomination that causes desolation[^12] is set up, there will be 1,290 days.
וּמֵעֵת֙ הוּסַ֣ר הַתָּמִ֔יד וְלָתֵ֖ת שִׁקּ֣וּץ שֹׁמֵ֑ם יָמִ֕ים אֶ֖לֶף מָאתַ֥יִם וְתִשְׁעִֽים׃
Blessed is the one who waits and reaches 1,335 days.[^13]
אַשְׁרֵ֥י הַֽמְחַכֶּ֖ה וְיַגִּ֑יעַ לְיָמִ֕ים אֶ֕לֶף שְׁלֹ֥שׁ מֵא֖וֹת שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים וַחֲמִשָּֽׁה׃
But you, go your way to the end. You will rest, and you will rise to receive your allotted share at the end of the days."[^14]
וְאַתָּ֖ה לֵ֣ךְ לַקֵּ֑ץ וְתָנ֛וּחַ וְתַעֲמֹ֥ד לְגֹרָלְךָ֖ לְקֵ֥ץ הַיָּמִֽין׃

n.1: Literally "who stands over the sons of your people". See 10:13, 21.
n.2: Compare Exodus 32:32–33; Psalm 69:29 (69:28 in most English Bibles); Malachi 3:16; Revelation 20:12.
n.3: Literally "the ground of dust". Compare Genesis 3:19.
n.4: This is the clearest statement in the Old Testament of a resurrection of the dead (compare Isaiah 26:19). "Many" may mean a great number, or it may mean that not all will rise. Hebrew *dir'on*, "contempt, abhorrence", is found elsewhere only in Isaiah 66:24. Compare John 5:28–29.
n.6: Literally "the brightness of the dome", Hebrew *raqia*, the sky pictured as a solid vault (Genesis 1:6–8).
n.7: The Septuagint reads "and the land will be filled with injustice".
n.8: Hebrew *ye'or*, a word usually used of the Nile; here the Tigris (10:4). Also in verses 6–7.
n.9: That is, probably three and a half years. See 7:25.
n.10: Literally "the hand of the holy people". Compare Revelation 10:5–7.
n.12: Hebrew *shiqquts shomem*. See 11:31; compare 9:27 and Mark 13:14.
n.13: The numbers in verses 11 and 12 differ from each other and from 8:14. Each is a little more than three and a half years (compare verse 7).
n.14: Literally "and you will stand for your lot at the end of the days". *Rest* may refer to death and *rise* to resurrection (compare verse 2).
